oneOf.description: The account exists but its owner has not set a password yet. Allowed through: without a password there is nothing to sign in with, and once one is set the account is in use.

UserTyp.description:
Mirror of the `enterprise.user_typ` PostgreSQL enum (migration 021).

Lifting `user.typ` from a stringly-typed column to a real enum gets us: - DB-level whitelist (insert/update of an unknown variant fails). - Compile-time exhaustive matching at every read site (was previously ad-hoc `matches!(s.as_str(), "Admin" | "Sys")` in `role_resolver`/`tx_helper`/`admin_rbac`).

add_when.description:
When the account was created — the AUDIT block's "Created" field.

`add_when` is NOT NULL on both `enterprise.user` and tenant-manager's `user`, so this is `Option` to tolerate a projection that did not select it, not because a created account can lack a creation time.

Added late, and the reason is worth keeping: migration 317 put "Created" on the detail form reading `add_when`, but this struct — the only thing the `is_rpc` BIO's `get_user` path can return — never carried the column, so the field rendered permanently blank. The form was right; the projection was short.

password_age_days.description: "Password age" for the AUDIT block — derived from `pwd_changed_at`, in whole days. **Not a database column**: `#[field(skip)]` keeps it out of the SELECT projection (`sea_column_refs`), and `#[sqlx(default)]` keeps `derive(FromRow)` from trying to read a `password_age_days` column that doesn't exist. Populated by `UserBy::finish_computed_fields`, which every `UserBmc` fetch path calls — see there. `None` whenever `pwd_changed_at` is `None`; never a misleading `0`.

methods.name: supervisor_override_grant

params.name: meta

oneOf.description: Bare override code (receipt / dimensionless).
Move override pair (dimension code + hold-code subject).

params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

AckToken.description:
One acknowledgement unit on the move / directed-putaway override contract: a `(code, subject)` pair. `code` is the dimension — a `move_warning_codes` constant (source-loc hold 83, dest-loc hold 84, source-stock hold 80, …), or for receipt a bare `ReceiptValidationReturnCode`. `subject` is WHAT was overridden: the hold code string (`QcQuarantine`), or a rule id (directed putaway). The pair is atomic — `(83, X) != (84, X)` — so acking a hold on the source location never clears the same code on the destination.

Wire tolerance (contract `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-move-ack-override-contract.md`): the shared `CommandMeta.acknowledged_overrides` carries acks for BOTH receipt (bare integer codes, no subject) and move (pairs). This type deserializes EITHER form — a bare `27` becomes `{code: 27, subject: ""}`; an object `{"code":83,"subject":"QcQuarantine"}` keeps both — so an existing receipt client sending `[27, 71]` is unaffected while move sends `[{code, subject}]`. Serialization is always the canonical object form (the error envelope's `context.pairs`). Subject `""` is the receipt / dimensionless convention.

pairs.description: The pairs this grant authorizes. For a move: exactly what the refused move reported in `error.data.detail.context.pairs`. For a receipt override, likewise what the refused receipt command reported there: `{"code": 71, "subject": "receipt:<receipt_id>"}` for a close — bound to that receipt — and `{"code": <28|27>, "subject": "receipt:<receipt_id>/line:<receipt_detail_id>"}` for a shortage or excess — bound to that one line.

reason.description: Why the authorizer is allowing it. REQUIRED for a count-freeze pair (`{"code": 87, "subject": "count:<inventory_count_id>"}`): the owner asked for that reason to be recorded, and it is written onto the count as the mark that stock moved underneath it. Optional for every other pair, which says what it overrode in its own subject.

username.description: Required only when the caller cannot authorize every pair themselves.

methods.summary: Mint a supervisor override grant for the pairs a refused command reported. The grant binds OPERATOR + PAIRS + the authenticated authorizer, is single-use and expires in minutes. A move passes its id as move_execute's ctx.override_grant_id; receipt_close, receipt_receive_against_asn and receipt_receive_case_level_line take it as override_grant_id (meta or data). Receipt pairs are bound to what they decide: a close (71) to one receipt, {code, subject: "receipt:<receipt_id>"}; a shortage or excess (28/27) to one line, {code, subject: "receipt:<receipt_id>/line:<receipt_detail_id>"} — a grant for one line is refused on any other. Authority is checked PER PAIR: a move pair needs an override role (SUPERVISOR/MANAGER/ADMIN); a receipt pair needs the capability its code names (71 receipt.override_close_discrepancy, 28 receipt.override_qty_shortage, 27 receipt.override_qty_excess — SUPERVISOR only), so an ADMIN or MANAGER cannot authorize a receipt override. A caller who holds every pair's authority mints seamlessly with no credentials; anyone else must supply username + password, verified through the same path as /api/login, and that person is held to the same per-pair rule. Supplying credentials always authenticates THEM, even if the caller could have minted seamlessly. The recorded authorizer is whoever the SERVER authenticated here; it is never taken from the command request. A count-freeze pair ({code: 87, subject: "count:<inventory_count_id>"}), which a Hard inventory count's freeze reports in context.pairs, needs an override role like a move pair AND a reason: the reason is recorded on the grant and written onto the count as the mark that stock moved underneath it, so the counter knows the number is in doubt. Such a grant is refused without one. move_execute, inventory_adjustment_post (override_grant_id) and pick_commit (count_freeze_grant_id) redeem it.

schema.description:
Read-only audit log entry — **selected from `enterprise.audit_log_view`** (see ADR-025), not the raw `audit_log` table. DamageAction.description: Per Decisions Log D-26 + T-062 (migration 148). Action triggered by ReportDamage based on severity + OwnerConfig. The first three are the original on-report actions (just-record / hold-LPN / bump-qty-damaged). The four added in T-062 represent owner policy for auto-routing damage to a final disposition without manual intervention: * WriteOff  — auto-call WriteOffDamage on report (decrement inventory). * RTV       — auto-call MoveDamageToRtv on report (move to RTV staging). * Repurpose — flag disposition='Repurpose' (Phase 2 wires SKU substitute). * Destroy   — flag disposition='Destroyed' (Phase 3 wires regulated paths).

InventoryTrackingGranularity.description:
ADR-046 D-69b — per-receipt inventory tracking granularity. Frozen at receipt creation, never changes after.

- **Aggregate** (default) — pre-case-level behaviour: scan pallet, type qty, single inventory_balances row per pallet. Status quo for non-regulated owners. - **Pallet** — operator scans every case (audit trail in receipt_detail_case) but inventory_balances stays per-pallet. - **Case** — every case becomes its own inventory_balances row. Full case-level traceability for pharma / food / regulated industries.

Stored as PG enum `inventory_tracking_granularity` (created in migration 126).

confirm_empty_on_move.description: Count spec Appendix L (wms-app 116): a manual move that takes the last stock of this owner out of its source location asks the operator whether the location is empty.

default_discard_loc.description: E.2 (migration 162). Discard-condition returns deposit destination. NULL → write-off without deposit (current behavior, no inventory row); set → deposit through DepositService into this loc.

default_receiving_loc.description: Миграция 350. Ячейка, которую окно приёмки подставляет по умолчанию. NULL = не задана: оператор выбирает сам, как выбирал до 350.

default_rtv_loc.description: T-062 (migration 148). Falls back to `default_returns_loc` when NULL; if both NULL, MoveDamageToRtv returns NoRtvLocConfigured error.

putaway_reservation_ttl_min.description:
Minutes a directed-putaway location reservation (`inventory_pending_move_in`) is held for this owner's stock before the TTL sweeper releases it.

`None` is not "no TTL": it means INHERIT, and `PendingMoveInBmc::resolve_ttl_minutes` falls through to the `system_settings` key `PUTAWAY_RESERVATION_TTL_MIN`. Owner-level because the number is really a walking distance — a deep warehouse needs a longer hold than a two-aisle one.

`chk_owner_config_putaway_ttl` forbids 0 and negatives: a reservation born already expired is not a short hold, it is an insert that always fails (`chk_inventory_pending_move_in_expiry_after_add`).

rtv_gl_account_hint.description: T-062 (migration 148). ERP GL account hint passed in `damage.rtv_initiated` outbox event (e.g. SAP `1450-RTV-Receivable`).

write_off_gl_account_hint.description: T-062 (migration 148). ERP GL account hint passed in `damage.written_off` outbox event. ERP may use directly or map through its own table.

SkuRotation.description:
Represents SKU rotation policy, determining the order in which stock is picked.

- `Fifo`: First-In-First-Out rotation. - `Lifo`: Last-In-First-Out rotation.

Used to specify how items are rotated in inventory management.

# Examples

``` use crate::model::sku::SkuRotation; let rotation = SkuRotation::Fifo; assert_eq!(rotation.to_string(), "Fifo"); ``` `PartialEq`/`Eq` are unconditional (not `cfg(test)`): a putaway step now compares `SkuRotation` values outside tests too, via `PropRule::matches` (phase 2b product criteria).

Minutes a directed-putaway location reservation (`inventory_pending_move_in`) is held for this owner's stock before the TTL sweeper releases it.

`None` is not "no TTL": it means INHERIT, and `PendingMoveInBmc::resolve_ttl_minutes` falls through to the `system_settings` key `PUTAWAY_RESERVATION_TTL_MIN`. Owner-level because the number is really a walking distance — a deep warehouse needs a longer hold than a two-aisle one.

`chk_owner_config_putaway_ttl` forbids 0 and negatives: a reservation born already expired is not a short hold, it is an insert that always fails (`chk_inventory_pending_move_in_expiry_after_add`).

rtv_gl_account_hint.description: T-062 (migration 148). ERP GL account hint passed in `damage.rtv_initiated` outbox event (e.g. SAP `1450-RTV-Receivable`).

write_off_gl_account_hint.description: T-062 (migration 148). ERP GL account hint passed in `damage.written_off` outbox event. ERP may use directly or map through its own table.

Used to specify how items are rotated in inventory management.

InventoryTrackingGranularity.description:
ADR-046 D-69b — per-receipt inventory tracking granularity. Frozen at receipt creation, never changes after.

- **Aggregate** (default) — pre-case-level behaviour: scan pallet, type qty, single inventory_balances row per pallet. Status quo for non-regulated owners. - **Pallet** — operator scans every case (audit trail in receipt_detail_case) but inventory_balances stays per-pallet. - **Case** — every case becomes its own inventory_balances row. Full case-level traceability for pharma / food / regulated industries.

Stored as PG enum `inventory_tracking_granularity` (created in migration 126).

oneOf.description: The location of open discrete pick pallets (the pick-pallet wms-app migrations): goods on an operator's forks between the pick and the pallet's close. One per warehouse schema, seeded as `INTRANSIT`; outside every other door — allocation, putaway, move, adjustment, receiving, the location advisory.

A pack station (post-pick spec §6, D-47, D-49; wms-app 066/067): the location where picked units wait for Verify / Repack. Goods arrive only by the Outbound Flow Router's decision, so no putaway, manual move or allocation targets it; picked stock is delivered into it.
A consolidation station (consolidation H1; wms-app 20261021191020/1): the location where packed boxes are put onto outbound pallets. Goods arrive only by the router's decision; never allocated from.

oneOf.description: The location of open discrete pick pallets (the pick-pallet wms-app migrations): goods on an operator's forks between the pick and the pallet's close. One per warehouse schema, seeded as `INTRANSIT`; outside every other door — allocation, putaway, move, adjustment, receiving, the location advisory.

A pack station (post-pick spec §6, D-47, D-49; wms-app 066/067): the location where picked units wait for Verify / Repack. Goods arrive only by the Outbound Flow Router's decision, so no putaway, manual move or allocation targets it; picked stock is delivered into it.
A consolidation station (consolidation H1; wms-app 20261021191020/1): the location where packed boxes are put onto outbound pallets. Goods arrive only by the router's decision; never allocated from.

schema.description:
Represents a Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), the core entity for inventory items.

Each SKU contains information about the item, its ownership, packaging, classification, fulfillment parameters, and policy references. Timestamps track creation and modification.

# Fields - `id`: Unique SKU identifier. - `external_id`: Optional external reference. - `owner_id`: Owner's identifier. - `code`: SKU code, unique per owner. - `descr`: Description of the SKU. - `pack_id`: Reference to packaging. - `gross_wgt`, `net_wgt`, `cube`: Physical characteristics. - `abc`: ABC rotation speed classification. - `class`, `active`, `sku_group`: Classification and grouping. - `*_policy_id`: Various policy references (allocation, replenishment, etc.). - `on_rec_copy_receipt_number`: Copy receipt number on receipt. - `putaway_loc`, `putawayzone`, `receipt_qc_loc`: Putaway Location details. - `putaway_class`: Putaway class. - `rotation`: SKU rotation policy. - `shelf_life`, `min_shelf_life_on_pick`, `min_shelf_life_on_rec`: Shelf life parameters. - `receipt_hold_code`, `expire_days`, `deliver_by_days`, `best_by_days`: Expiry and delivery codes. - `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn`: Allow multiple lots on license plate number. - `force_separate_lpn_per_lot`: This SKU demands its own container per lot. - `add_who`, `add_when`, `mod_who`, `mod_when`: Audit fields for creation and modification.

force_separate_lpn_per_lot.description: The same prohibition as `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn = false`, asked of the ARRIVING SKU instead of the ones already on the pallet. See [`DEFAULT_FORCE_SEPARATE_LPN_PER_LOT`] for why both exist.

pick_instruction.description: Standing pick instruction for this item (wms-app 044): shown on every pick of it and acknowledged before the pick commits (RF `PICKINS`).

positions_required.description: How many adjacent positions of one section this item occupies. `1` is an ordinary item; more means the whole section must be free and its dimensions are measured together.

stack_limit.description: How high this item may be stacked, whatever the rack allows. `0` is no opinion; the engine takes the minimum of this and `location.stack_limit`, so an item may lower the rack's limit and never raise it.

allow_deferred_capture.description: Explicit permission to receive inventory before serial capture is complete. Deliberately separate from `allow_receive_capture`, which merely enables capture at the receive checkpoint.

continuous_serial_tracking.description: Master flag. If false — other fields ignored.

pick_episode_reassignment_mode.description: Behaviour when a different operator resumes a Pick with an unfinished serial episode.

serial_scope.description: Migration 153 — serial granularity. Tells receive_against_asn / capture_serial how to compute `serials_to_collect_qty` from the operator's submitted qty: - `PerUnit`      → 1 serial per atomic EA (qty_base from pack hierarchy) - `PerCase`      → 1 serial per submitted UOM (typical SSCC) - `PerPallet`    → 1 serial per pack_item.uom='PL' tier - `PerInnerPack` → 1 serial per pack_item.uom='IP' tier Default `PerUnit`. Stored as VARCHAR with CHECK constraint.

schema.description:
Represents a Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), the core entity for inventory items.

Each SKU contains information about the item, its ownership, packaging, classification, fulfillment parameters, and policy references. Timestamps track creation and modification.

# Fields - `id`: Unique SKU identifier. - `external_id`: Optional external reference. - `owner_id`: Owner's identifier. - `code`: SKU code, unique per owner. - `descr`: Description of the SKU. - `pack_id`: Reference to packaging. - `gross_wgt`, `net_wgt`, `cube`: Physical characteristics. - `abc`: ABC rotation speed classification. - `class`, `active`, `sku_group`: Classification and grouping. - `*_policy_id`: Various policy references (allocation, replenishment, etc.). - `on_rec_copy_receipt_number`: Copy receipt number on receipt. - `putaway_loc`, `putawayzone`, `receipt_qc_loc`: Putaway Location details. - `putaway_class`: Putaway class. - `rotation`: SKU rotation policy. - `shelf_life`, `min_shelf_life_on_pick`, `min_shelf_life_on_rec`: Shelf life parameters. - `receipt_hold_code`, `expire_days`, `deliver_by_days`, `best_by_days`: Expiry and delivery codes. - `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn`: Allow multiple lots on license plate number. - `force_separate_lpn_per_lot`: This SKU demands its own container per lot. - `add_who`, `add_when`, `mod_who`, `mod_when`: Audit fields for creation and modification.

force_separate_lpn_per_lot.description: The same prohibition as `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn = false`, asked of the ARRIVING SKU instead of the ones already on the pallet. See [`DEFAULT_FORCE_SEPARATE_LPN_PER_LOT`] for why both exist.

pick_instruction.description: Standing pick instruction for this item (wms-app 044): shown on every pick of it and acknowledged before the pick commits (RF `PICKINS`).

positions_required.description: How many adjacent positions of one section this item occupies. `1` is an ordinary item; more means the whole section must be free and its dimensions are measured together.

stack_limit.description: How high this item may be stacked, whatever the rack allows. `0` is no opinion; the engine takes the minimum of this and `location.stack_limit`, so an item may lower the rack's limit and never raise it.

oneOf.description: Как было до миграции 351: искать партию по атрибутам, и завести новую только если ничего не подошло. Два физически разных прихода с одинаковыми атрибутами попадают в ОДНУ партию.
Одна партия на приёмку: все приёмы одного документа кладутся в неё.
Своя партия на КАЖДЫЙ физический приход. Остатки разных приходов не сольются: партия входит в ключ слияния наравне с владельцем, товаром, упаковкой, единицей, ячейкой и контейнером.
The operator cannot check this value on the floor; the card may show it, nothing is asked.
The operator compares the value printed on the goods with the card.
The value is read from a barcode on the goods.
Either of the two.

lot_creation.description:
КОГДА рождается новая партия (миграция 351).

Это единственное место, где такое решение записано. До 351 его не принимал никто: партия бралась по совпадению атрибутов, и совпадение молча означало «это тот же товар из того же прихода».

show_on_pick_manufactured_date.description: Shown on the pick card (spec 2026-10-04 §8). Only a date captured on receipt can be shown: `chk_lot_policy_pick_dates_need_receipt`.

verification_manufactured_date.description: How the operator can check the date on the goods. Anything but `NotVerifiable` needs the date shown on pick: `chk_lot_policy_verified_dates_are_shown`.

InventoryTrackingGranularity.description:
ADR-046 D-69b — per-receipt inventory tracking granularity. Frozen at receipt creation, never changes after.

- **Aggregate** (default) — pre-case-level behaviour: scan pallet, type qty, single inventory_balances row per pallet. Status quo for non-regulated owners. - **Pallet** — operator scans every case (audit trail in receipt_detail_case) but inventory_balances stays per-pallet. - **Case** — every case becomes its own inventory_balances row. Full case-level traceability for pharma / food / regulated industries.

Stored as PG enum `inventory_tracking_granularity` (created in migration 126).

In WMS terms, an RMA receipt refers to the process of receiving returned goods into the warehouse that were previously shipped to a customer. It is a structured way to handle customer returns.

schema.description:
What a client may change on a receipt header: reference, party and planning data, and nothing the receipt is judged by.

Deliberately NOT [`ReceiptForUpdate`]. That struct carries `status`, `completion`, `close_summary` and `cancel_summary` — correctly, because Close, Cancel, PutOnHold and ReleaseFromHold write them — and handing it to the wire turned the generic CRUD update into a second, unguarded way to move a receipt:

```text update_receipt{ status: "Closed", completion: "Full" } → 200 OK ```

No state machine, no version, and no summary of what happened: a receipt could be closed with no `close_summary`, cancelled with no `cancel_summary`, or pulled back out of a terminal state into `Open`. `update_receipt` is granted to OPERATOR by the seeder's operational-entity rule, so it was not even an admin-only hole. Same shape as the line-level hole PR #436 closed — this is the half it left open.

The fields are absent by CONSTRUCTION rather than filtered at runtime: one that cannot be deserialized cannot be reintroduced by someone extending a mapping function. They move only through their own commands.

Also absent, each for its own reason: - `owner_id`, `receipt_number` — identity, fixed when the receipt is created. - `close_date` — stamped by Close, alongside the summary it belongs to.

`deny_unknown_fields` is the point, not a detail: serde's default is to IGNORE what it does not know, so a client sending `status: "Closed"` would get `200 OK` and a response showing the old status — the write silently dropped, the caller convinced it landed. For the field the whole lifecycle turns on, refusing loudly is the only honest answer.

Receipt.description:
## 'RMA' Field: Return Merchandise Authorization,

In WMS terms, an RMA receipt refers to the process of receiving returned goods into the warehouse that were previously shipped to a customer. It is a structured way to handle customer returns.

# Key Aspects of RMA in WMS | Aspect | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Purpose** | To manage and track the return of products from customers or stores. | | **Authorization** | Usually issued by a customer service or sales system before the return. | | **Receipt Type** | RMA receipts are often a **distinct type of inbound receipt**. | | **Validation** | WMS verifies returned items against the authorized RMA before receiving. | | **Disposition** | Returned items may be **restocked**, **scrapped**, or **quarantined**. |

LotAttrCheckMode.description:
Per-line lot-attributes validation mode. Replaces the legacy pair of `match_lot_attributes: Option<bool>` (D-27) and `match_lot_attributes_strict: bool` (D-65 / ADR-050) with a single 3-state enum so the four-flag-combinations (one of which was a nonsensical `null + strict`) are no longer representable.

- `Disabled` — no validation; any scanned lot_attrs accepted as-is. Cascade tier 1 also stays lenient: an empty expected set on a candidate accumulates the operator's scan into that line. - `Advisory` — validation runs against expected lot_attrs; per-attribute supervisor overrides through `lot_policy_attribute.override_allowed` (D-27 / RPV code 36) are honoured. - `Strict` — ASN-pre-bound lot (pharma, EDI 856 contracts). `set_equal(expected, scanned)` is required. No overrides (RPV code 34, non-overridable).

container_id.description: The EXPECTED LPN — the container the supplier announced the goods on. hold_code.description: Hold code at receive time — VARCHAR mirroring `inv_hold_code` enum values (e.g. `Damaged`, `QcRequired`, `CustomerReturn`). NULL when the line carries no auto-hold. Filled by the receive command per flow: damage receive → `Damaged`, return condition=NeedsRefurb → `QcRequired`, etc. Audit-only on the line; the actual ATP-blocking hold lives in `inventory_hold` on the LPN / location.

qty_damaged.description: Per Decisions Log D-26 (ReportDamage Reject action) and D-05 (completion algorithm).

target_disposition.description: Per Decisions Log D-36. Stock | CrossDock | Hold. Default Stock.

to_container_id.description: The ACTUAL LPN — the container receive put the goods into (the supplier's, or one the operator minted). NULL until the first receive, and for loose stock. Anything that acts on the goods reads this, not `container_id`.

uom_received.description: ADR-045 §1 — native UOM as entered by the operator at receive time (e.g. "CS" when receiving 10 cases of 24 EA each). `qty_received` always stays in base units. Native qty is derivable from `qty_received / pack_item.base_qty WHERE pack_id, uom = uom_received`.

methods.summary: Receipt envelope: header + lines + last audit row in one roundtrip

methods.name: get_sku_envelope

owner_code.description: Business owner code (e.g. "OWNER002"). Used by RCBLIND01 / any flow where the operator scans / picks by code rather than id. Server resolves to `owner_id` via OwnerBmc lookup; not-found → typed Validation error. Exactly one of (`owner_id`, `owner_code`) is required.

owner_id.description: Numeric owner id. Preferred when the caller already has it (RCASN01SKU resolves it via the ASN lookup). Mutually exclusive with `owner_code` — `owner_id` wins when both are supplied.

receipt_id.description: Optional receipt context. When the SKU is scanned *against an ASN* (RCASN01SKU passes `display.receipt_id`), the envelope resolves the matching receipt line and pre-fills / locks its expected lot attributes (ADR-050). Blind receive (RCBLIND01) omits it → plain prompt, no pre-fill.

AbcRotationSpeed.description:
Loc/Sku Abc - dependent type, code_list_value

`PartialEq`/`Eq` are unconditional (not `cfg(test)`) because `CandidateFilter::loc_abc` (phase 2a) holds a `PropRule<AbcRotationSpeed>`, and `CandidateFilter` derives `PartialEq, Eq` outside test code too.

LotAttributePrompt.description: One operator-facing lot-attribute slot on a receive line screen, with the ASN-expected pre-fill and strict-lock resolved (ADR-050). Wire DTO — not a `lot_policy_attribute` row.

is_date.description:
`true` → this slot is a DATE, not free text: one of the four date columns `lot_policy` carries (`DATE_ATTRIBUTE_CODES`), folded in as a synthetic slot so RF and the web prompt for it alongside the custom attributes.

The server has always known this and never said it, so every renderer drew a text box and the operator typed a date into it by hand — `parse_date` then accepted or silently dropped whatever arrived. The flag does not change what is sent (still a string in `lot_attributes`); it lets a screen offer the right control for it.

readonly.description: `true` → operator may not edit. The line is strict-match (D-65) AND there is an expected value to enforce. Blank slots stay editable even on a strict line (nothing to lock).

value.description: ASN-expected value for this attribute on the scanned line, when the line carries one. `None` → blank input.

is_active.description: ADR-045 §3 — append-only convention. UI dropdowns filter to `is_active=true`; FK lookups from receipt_detail / inventory_balances* continue to resolve regardless. Editing a pack means inserting a new row + flipping the old one's flag, not UPDATE-ing master values.

rotation_rule.description: Как этот уровень разрешено поворачивать при укладке в коробку. Правило стоит здесь, а не на товаре: в коробку кладут упаковку, и «этой стороной вверх» пишут на ней.

ship_as_is.description: Explicit factory packaging. Mutually exclusive with `cartonize`.

PutawayClass.description: `PartialEq`/`Eq` are unconditional (not `cfg(test)`): a putaway step now compares `PutawayClass` values outside tests too, via `PropRule::matches` (phase 2b product criteria).

oneOf.description: Все шесть ориентаций.
Только естественное положение.
«Этой стороной вверх».

SerialParseMode.description: Per Decisions Log D-32. How serial is extracted from a scanned barcode.

Sku.description:
Represents a Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), the core entity for inventory items.

Each SKU contains information about the item, its ownership, packaging, classification, fulfillment parameters, and policy references. Timestamps track creation and modification.

# Fields - `id`: Unique SKU identifier. - `external_id`: Optional external reference. - `owner_id`: Owner's identifier. - `code`: SKU code, unique per owner. - `descr`: Description of the SKU. - `pack_id`: Reference to packaging. - `gross_wgt`, `net_wgt`, `cube`: Physical characteristics. - `abc`: ABC rotation speed classification. - `class`, `active`, `sku_group`: Classification and grouping. - `*_policy_id`: Various policy references (allocation, replenishment, etc.). - `on_rec_copy_receipt_number`: Copy receipt number on receipt. - `putaway_loc`, `putawayzone`, `receipt_qc_loc`: Putaway Location details. - `putaway_class`: Putaway class. - `rotation`: SKU rotation policy. - `shelf_life`, `min_shelf_life_on_pick`, `min_shelf_life_on_rec`: Shelf life parameters. - `receipt_hold_code`, `expire_days`, `deliver_by_days`, `best_by_days`: Expiry and delivery codes. - `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn`: Allow multiple lots on license plate number. - `force_separate_lpn_per_lot`: This SKU demands its own container per lot. - `add_who`, `add_when`, `mod_who`, `mod_when`: Audit fields for creation and modification.

force_separate_lpn_per_lot.description: The same prohibition as `allow_multi_lot_on_lpn = false`, asked of the ARRIVING SKU instead of the ones already on the pallet. See [`DEFAULT_FORCE_SEPARATE_LPN_PER_LOT`] for why both exist.

pick_instruction.description: Standing pick instruction for this item (wms-app 044): shown on every pick of it and acknowledged before the pick commits (RF `PICKINS`).

positions_required.description: How many adjacent positions of one section this item occupies. `1` is an ordinary item; more means the whole section must be free and its dimensions are measured together.

stack_limit.description: How high this item may be stacked, whatever the rack allows. `0` is no opinion; the engine takes the minimum of this and `location.stack_limit`, so an item may lower the rack's limit and never raise it.

SkuRotation.description:
Represents SKU rotation policy, determining the order in which stock is picked.

- `Fifo`: First-In-First-Out rotation. - `Lifo`: Last-In-First-Out rotation.

Used to specify how items are rotated in inventory management.

# Examples

``` use crate::model::sku::SkuRotation; let rotation = SkuRotation::Fifo; assert_eq!(rotation.to_string(), "Fifo"); ``` `PartialEq`/`Eq` are unconditional (not `cfg(test)`): a putaway step now compares `SkuRotation` values outside tests too, via `PropRule::matches` (phase 2b product criteria).

allow_deferred_capture.description: Explicit permission to receive inventory before serial capture is complete. Deliberately separate from `allow_receive_capture`, which merely enables capture at the receive checkpoint.

continuous_serial_tracking.description: Master flag. If false — other fields ignored.

pick_episode_reassignment_mode.description: Behaviour when a different operator resumes a Pick with an unfinished serial episode.

serial_scope.description: Migration 153 — serial granularity. Tells receive_against_asn / capture_serial how to compute `serials_to_collect_qty` from the operator's submitted qty: - `PerUnit`      → 1 serial per atomic EA (qty_base from pack hierarchy) - `PerCase`      → 1 serial per submitted UOM (typical SSCC) - `PerPallet`    → 1 serial per pack_item.uom='PL' tier - `PerInnerPack` → 1 serial per pack_item.uom='IP' tier Default `PerUnit`. Stored as VARCHAR with CHECK constraint.

barcodes.description: All active barcodes for this SKU. Empty Vec when none registered; caller can fall back to scanning by sku.code directly.

expected_lpn.description: The LPN RF prefills To LPN with: the supplier's expected LPN, when every open line of this SKU on the receipt that offers one offers the same one — a line offers its expected LPN unless it was already received into ANOTHER LPN. `None` when no line offers one, lines offer different ones, and on a blind scan (no `receipt_id`) — the operator scans the label and the cascade finds the line by it. Rule: `wms_inbound::service::receipt::expected_lpn`.

lot_policy_attributes.description: Lot-attribute prompt for this SKU (`show=true` attrs only). When the scan is against an ASN (`receipt_id` supplied + a matching line), each entry is pre-filled with the line's expected `value` and `readonly` on a Strict line (ADR-050); otherwise blank + editable. Empty when the SKU has no lot_policy. RF prompts the operator for these before submitting receive_blind / receive_against_asn — required attrs left unsupplied fail server-side validation.

owner_id.description: Resolved owner id. Always set on a successful response. Surfaced so callers that started with `owner_code` (RCBLIND01, slice C.5) can copy the numeric id into `display.owner_id` for the rest of the chain — the LINE call still wants i64 on the wire. Callers that already had `owner_id` (RCASN01SKU) can ignore the field.

pack.description: Default Pack tied to `sku.pack_id`. RF shows `pack.code` (or `pack.descr`) on receive screens so the operator sees a name instead of a meaningless integer. None only if the pack row vanished (referential-integrity break) — normal operation always returns it.

serial_config.description: Per-SKU serial-tracking configuration. None when no row exists yet — the SKU is not serial-tracked (or hasn't been configured).

methods.summary: SKU envelope: sku + serial_config + barcodes for receive-flow round-trip elimination

methods.name: assign_lpn

format_id.description: Catalog spec mentions a numeric `format_id`. Per Container Spec §3.3 + §5 the actual format is OwnerConfig.auto_generate_lpn_format (a string template) — not a numeric id. This field is accepted for backwards-compat with the catalog but currently ignored; generation uses the global `code_counter.container_code` sequence via `GenKey::get(CounterName::ContainerCode)` which is owner- agnostic and warehouse-scoped (per typed `Ctx::data_scope`).

qty.description: How many LPN codes to mint in this batch. `None` or `Some(0)` returns an empty Vec (no-op). `Some(n)` returns exactly n codes. Bulk-allocate when the operator is about to receive a multi-pallet shipment — saves N round-trips compared to calling once per pallet.

sku_id.description: Informational only — recorded in event payloads / audit when this becomes a tracked allocation. Today the SKU is not used by the generator but the API accepts it so callers can keep their payload stable through future enhancements.

lpns.description: Newly minted LPN codes, in the order they were drawn from the sequence. Each is a 10-char zero-padded numeric string — guaranteed unique within this warehouse schema and never reused.

methods.summary: Mint N fresh LPN codes from the warehouse container_code sequence (FOR-UPDATE-locked, no collisions)

methods.name: get_owner_damage_policy

owner_id.description: `owners.id` of the SKU's owner. Resolved upstream by the caller (e.g. `Receipt::owner_id` for a damage report tied to a receipt).

DamageAction.description: Per Decisions Log D-26 + T-062 (migration 148). Action triggered by ReportDamage based on severity + OwnerConfig. The first three are the original on-report actions (just-record / hold-LPN / bump-qty-damaged). The four added in T-062 represent owner policy for auto-routing damage to a final disposition without manual intervention: * WriteOff  — auto-call WriteOffDamage on report (decrement inventory). * RTV       — auto-call MoveDamageToRtv on report (move to RTV staging). * Repurpose — flag disposition='Repurpose' (Phase 2 wires SKU substitute). * Destroy   — flag disposition='Destroyed' (Phase 3 wires regulated paths).

OwnerDamagePolicy.description:
Damage routing policy for an owner's incoming inventory.

Sourced from `owner_config.damage_{minor|major|total}_action`. ReportDamage (Catalog 10) consults this row to decide what to do with a damaged unit: `None` (keep), `Hold` (release-blocked), or `Reject` (return to vendor).

Returned as a flat shape (no nested `OwnerConfig`) so RF clients don't pay the deserialization cost of fields they ignore.

user_id.description: Receipts created by this user (`receipt.add_who`). RF "my work" view filters by the operator's id; supervisors pass another user id to peek at someone else's queue.

warehouse_id.description: Warehouse scope is already implicit in `Ctx.wh_schema` — the row list is restricted to that schema's `receipt` table. The id is accepted on the input so callers can keep their payload symmetric with other RF endpoints; it is not currently used in the WHERE clause (the schema bind is sufficient).

InventoryTrackingGranularity.description:
ADR-046 D-69b — per-receipt inventory tracking granularity. Frozen at receipt creation, never changes after.

- **Aggregate** (default) — pre-case-level behaviour: scan pallet, type qty, single inventory_balances row per pallet. Status quo for non-regulated owners. - **Pallet** — operator scans every case (audit trail in receipt_detail_case) but inventory_balances stays per-pallet. - **Case** — every case becomes its own inventory_balances row. Full case-level traceability for pharma / food / regulated industries.

Stored as PG enum `inventory_tracking_granularity` (created in migration 126).

Receipt.description:
## 'RMA' Field: Return Merchandise Authorization,

In WMS terms, an RMA receipt refers to the process of receiving returned goods into the warehouse that were previously shipped to a customer. It is a structured way to handle customer returns.

# Key Aspects of RMA in WMS | Aspect | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Purpose** | To manage and track the return of products from customers or stores. | | **Authorization** | Usually issued by a customer service or sales system before the return. | | **Receipt Type** | RMA receipts are often a **distinct type of inbound receipt**. | | **Validation** | WMS verifies returned items against the authorized RMA before receiving. | | **Disposition** | Returned items may be **restocked**, **scrapped**, or **quarantined**. |

ReceiptHoldEvent.description:
Audit-trail entry surfaced for the receipt OnHold timeline.

Sourced from `receipt_audit` rows where `field_name='status'` and either `old_value='OnHold'` or `new_value='OnHold'` — i.e. transitions into or out of the hold state. Returned in chronological order so the UI can render a simple timeline ("placed on hold by U at T1, released by V at T2").

Note: this surfaces *receipt-level* status changes, not the deeper per-balance `inventory_hold` rows (those are cross-cutting and hard to attribute to a single receipt without a transaction-log walk — out of scope here).

direction.description: `"placed"` when transitioning *into* OnHold, `"released"` when transitioning *out of* OnHold. Lets the UI choose the right icon without re-checking old/new values client-side.

methods.summary: Receipt OnHold history (place/release events) sourced from receipt_audit status field

methods.name: get_receipt_detail_history

ReceiptDetailHistoryEvent.description:
One historical event for a receipt_detail line. Combines two upstream sources into a single timeline:

- **`audit`**: `receipt_audit` row tied to the parent receipt. Header audit covers status changes (Open→InProgress→OnHold→Closed) and completion transitions that affect this line indirectly. - **`txn`**: `transaction_log` row whose `source_code` matches the parent receipt's `receipt_number` and whose `sku_code` matches the detail line's SKU. This is the inventory-level evidence (deposits into a bin, hold placements, etc.) that the detail line generated.

We do NOT have a `receipt_detail_audit` table today, so this is the closest thing to a per-line history. UI can group by `event_kind`.

label.description: For `audit`: the field that changed (e.g. `status`, `completion`). For `txn`: the transaction_type code (e.g. `Receive`, `Hold`).

methods.summary: Per-line history: header audit + matching transaction_log entries (no detail-audit table; this is the closest available)

count.description: Optional count when the blocker is plural (for example, three unresolved episodes).

OpenEpisodeBrief.description: Minimal episode shape — only the fields RF needs for the resume branch (id + detail context + progress counters).

inventory_tracking_granularity.description: `receipt.inventory_tracking_granularity` (`Aggregate` | `Pallet` | `Case`). RCCASE01 (case-level entry screen) reads this to decide whether to push the case-scan loop or surface a typed error ("ASN is Aggregate — use Receive Against ASN instead"). RCASN01 ignores it (Aggregate is the implicit default).

open_episode.description: First Open / InProgress / AwaitingConfirmation serial-capture episode attached to any detail of this receipt, if any. Null when none. RCASN01 / RCASN01SUM check this on entry / resume to surface the spec §10.13 recovery flow — re-route the operator straight into RCSN01 with prior progress instead of restarting capture.

version.description:
OCC version (per CLAUDE.md classifier rules) — receipt is a stateful entity, downstream commands (`receipt_close` / `receipt_cancel` / `receipt_adjust_received_qty`) carry this on submit. RCASN01's `onResponseReceive.set` reads `response.version → display.receipt_version`; without it the rule silently resolved to undefined and any later stateful_command was sent without OCC protection.

Lives on `AsnDetails`, NOT on `AsnHeader`, because only the "read full ASN to operate on it" path needs the version. The F2 picker (`lookup_asn`/`search_asns`) lists candidates only — the operator picks one and then the flow fetches details via `get_asn_by_number`. Exposing version on every picker row was the "version just in case from frontend" anti-pattern.

The picker used to receive the parts — location, SKUs, quantity — and join them itself, which meant the dialog held the separator, and a separator is text a person reads. params.name: meta

oneOf.description: Bare override code (receipt / dimensionless).
Move override pair (dimension code + hold-code subject).

params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

oneOf.description: Migration 160 — cosmetic damage (scratch / dent on the packaging); the goods are sold without a discount. Default action on this severity is `None` — the goods go into normal stock with an audit-record for statistics.
No container — loose units.
Resolve an existing container by code.
Create a fresh top-level pallet. `code=None` triggers auto-generation per `OwnerConfig.auto_generate_lpn_format`.
Create a new case, optionally nested under an existing pallet.
Add a new case as child of an existing pallet.
Cross-dock staging container (Phase 2 cross-dock; outbound order ref).

damage_info.description: UC-RCV-09 — ASN F4 damage hot-key sub-flow. When the operator inside an ASN summary marks goods as damaged, RF sends nested DamageInfo here. Auto-fired ReportDamage attaches the audit row to the synth-line that the cascade lookup creates for unplanned damaged units. (Planned-line UPDATE path doesn't propagate yet — rare in practice; tracked as a follow-up.)

external_lot.description: Supplier-side lot ID scanned by the operator (cascade tier 4). Optional — most receives don't carry one.

override_grant_id.description: A supervisor's grant (`supervisor_override_grant`) authorising a capability-gated override on the LINE this receive books onto — a shortage (28) or an excess (27) — for an operator who does not hold the capability. Its pairs must be `{code, subject: "receipt:<receipt_id>/line:<receipt_detail_id>"}`, where the line is the one the cascade resolves this scan to; a refused receive names that exact pair in `context.pairs`. A receive that opens a new (synthetic) line cannot be authorised by grant. The authoriser recorded is the grant's, never a field of this request. Optional: a caller who holds the capability keeps acknowledging with the bare code in `acknowledged_overrides`, exactly as before. See `shared::override_grant`.

sku_code.description: SKU code from the operator's scan — the cascade keys on it. Mandatory: per ADR-047 the receive API takes business-level identifiers only (no `receipt_detail_id` leaks). The system resolves to a target `receipt_detail` row internally via `cascade_lookup`, or creates a synthetic line when no open ASN line matches.

target_container.description: Phase 4 — preferred container intent. Resolved to a container_id at the deposit/event boundary via `ContainerService::resolve_or_create`. When `None`, the command falls back to `to_lpn` (legacy path).

to_lpn.description: Legacy LPN-string input (Phase 1-3). Still accepted for backward compatibility; ignored when `target_container` is populated.

uom_received.description: ADR-045 §1 — operator-entered native UOM. For ASN flow, falls back to `receipt_detail.uom` (line-level expected) → `sku.default_uom`.

HoldInfo.description: Per Decisions Log D-28. Auto-hold instruction emitted by validators (NOT an error). Returned to RF in command Output structs so client knows what holds were applied.

OpenEpisodeState.description:
The capture episode as it stands after this receive folded into it.

Named like the shapes the wire already carries for exactly this purpose — `OpenEpisodeBrief` on `get_asn_by_number` and `OpenEpisodeRow` on `list_open_episodes_for_receipt` — so a client reads one vocabulary wherever it meets an episode. Those two live in app-server, which a domain crate may not depend on, so the names travel rather than the type.

**Why the result must carry it.** `serials_to_collect_qty` is what THIS call owes. A second receive on the same line folds into the same episode (`ensure_open_episode_for_deferred_receive`), so the episode's total is the sum and its `captured_qty` may already be non-zero. A client drawing a progress panel from the receive answer had only the increment to read, and the web dialog opened it on "0 of <increment>" — an invented zero and the wrong total, both healing on the first scan because `capture_serial` answers with the episode's own numbers.

captured_qty.description: Serials already captured against this episode.

expected_qty.description: Serials the episode expects in total — the sum across every receive that folded into it, not this call's share.

ReceiptCompletion.description:
Receipt completion (qty fulfilment). Per Decisions Log D-05. **Separate** from status. Computed from the qty fields of the details and aggregated onto the header.

- `Pending`  — nothing received - `Partial`  — received less than expected - `Full`     — exactly as expected (or Full with qty_rejected/qty_damaged) - `Over`     — received more than expected

collect_serials.description: Backend-driven gate for the `RCSN01` serial-capture loop (ADR-062, G-12). `true` when the SKU is serial-tracked (`sku_serial_config.continuous_serial_tracking`) AND the operator did NOT pass `serial_numbers` inline on this call — i.e. the deferred capture flow is needed. holds_applied.description: D-28 — auto-holds applied to LPN during this receive. Empty if none.

open_episode.description: The capture episode this receive opened or folded into, with what it now holds in total. A progress panel reads THIS, never the increment above: a second receive on the same line sums into one episode.

owner_id.description: Owner that owns the just-received line. Surfaced so RCSN01 / its status bar can render `owner / sku / lot` without a second round-trip; future `capture_serial` validation will also cross- check the operator's session against this.

serials_to_collect_qty.description:
How many serials the operator must collect to satisfy the just- received line. `qty as u32` (floored — serial-tracked SKUs are always integer-unit). Zero when `collect_serials` is `false`.

THIS call's obligation. The episode may hold more — see `open_episode`.

sku_code.description: SKU code of the just-received line (matches `receipt_detail.sku`). Same rationale as `owner_id` — keeps the deferred loop screen self-sufficient.

sku_id.description: SKU primary key. Needed by clients that want to query `sku_serial_config` (anomaly thresholds, parse mode, etc.) without first resolving by code + owner.

Ключи объектов, которые оператор уже загрузил по подписанным ссылкам (`receipt_damage_photo_upload_url`). Ложатся в `receipt_detail_damage.photo_attachment_ids` В ТОЙ ЖЕ ТРАНЗАКЦИИ, что и сама запись, — либо запись с фотографиями, либо ни то, ни другое.

Необязательны, и это не формальность: в макете фото «recommended», и повреждение записывается без них.

**Тип поля был `Option<Vec<i64>>`** — с Phase 1, где фотографии мыслились числовыми id вложений (колонку завела wms-app 084 как «Phase 2+ attachments»). Ключ объекта в S3 — строка, и в `i64` он не влезает; менять тип безопасно, потому что отправителя у поля никогда не было: во всех вызовах (включая `app_server_quick_dev`) оно `null`. Имя колонки осталось историческим — миграции под фото не требуется.

Каждый ключ проверяется на принадлежность ЭТОЙ строке приёмки ([`photo_column_for_line`]): значение приезжает от клиента, и без проверки к своему повреждению можно было бы прицепить чужую фотографию.

DamageAction.description: Per Decisions Log D-26 + T-062 (migration 148). Action triggered by ReportDamage based on severity + OwnerConfig. LotAttrCheckMode.description:
Per-line lot-attributes validation mode. Replaces the legacy pair of `match_lot_attributes: Option<bool>` (D-27) and `match_lot_attributes_strict: bool` (D-65 / ADR-050) with a single 3-state enum so the four-flag-combinations (one of which was a nonsensical `null + strict`) are no longer representable.

- `Disabled` — no validation; any scanned lot_attrs accepted as-is. Cascade tier 1 also stays lenient: an empty expected set on a candidate accumulates the operator's scan into that line. - `Advisory` — validation runs against expected lot_attrs; per-attribute supervisor overrides through `lot_policy_attribute.override_allowed` (D-27 / RPV code 36) are honoured. - `Strict` — ASN-pre-bound lot (pharma, EDI 856 contracts). `set_equal(expected, scanned)` is required. No overrides (RPV code 34, non-overridable).

ReceiptCompletion.description:
Receipt completion (qty fulfilment). Per Decisions Log D-05. **Separate** from status. Computed from the qty fields of the details and aggregated onto the header.

- `Pending`  — nothing received - `Partial`  — received less than expected - `Full`     — exactly as expected (or Full with qty_rejected/qty_damaged) - `Over`     — received more than expected

ReceiptStatus.description:
Receipt lifecycle status — 5 clean values. Per Decisions Log D-02. The old 8 values (New|InTransit|Scheduled|InReceiving|Received|Verified|Closed|Cancelled) were removed together with the old `execute_*` flow.

The same enum is used for `Receipt.status` and `ReceiptDetail.status` (D-03). Completeness — a separate field `completion: ReceiptCompletion` (D-05).

ReceiptTargetDisposition.description: Target disposition for received goods. Per Decisions Log D-36. Phase 1: always default `Stock`. Phase 2 cross-dock detection sets `CrossDock`. `Hold` — for QC-quarantine when auto-hold conditions are triggered.

LotAttributePrompt.description: One operator-facing lot-attribute slot on a receive line screen, with the ASN-expected pre-fill and strict-lock resolved (ADR-050). Wire DTO — not a `lot_policy_attribute` row.

is_date.description:
`true` → this slot is a DATE, not free text: one of the four date columns `lot_policy` carries (`DATE_ATTRIBUTE_CODES`), folded in as a synthetic slot so RF and the web prompt for it alongside the custom attributes.

The server has always known this and never said it, so every renderer drew a text box and the operator typed a date into it by hand — `parse_date` then accepted or silently dropped whatever arrived. The flag does not change what is sent (still a string in `lot_attributes`); it lets a screen offer the right control for it.

readonly.description: `true` → operator may not edit. The line is strict-match (D-65) AND there is an expected value to enforce. Blank slots stay editable even on a strict line (nothing to lock).

value.description: ASN-expected value for this attribute on the scanned line, when the line carries one. `None` → blank input.

PackUnit.description: One unit the SKU can be received in; `factor` base units make one.

ReceiveLimits.description: The over-receipt thresholds in THIS LINE's terms, in base units over the line's open quantity. `None` = no such threshold.

approval_possible.description: Between the two, a supervisor's approval (code 27) can clear it.

block_over_base.description: Beyond this, the owner refuses outright — no approval clears it.

soft_percent.description: The policy's percents, for the words ("within the +5% tolerance").

warn_over_base.description: Up to this much over, the receive saves (amber when over at all).

schema.description: The Receive dialog's read of one line.

default_location.description: Ячейка, с которой окно открывается, — `owner_config.default_receiving_loc` владельца строки (миграция 350). `None` = владелец её не назвал, и оператор выбирает сам.

lot_prompts.description: Exactly what RF prompts for (`build_prompts`), for THIS line.

packs.description: Smallest first. Empty when the pack has no usable item.

schema.description:
What a client may change on a receipt line: reference and planning data, and nothing the receipt is judged by.

Deliberately NOT [`ReceiptDetailForUpdate`]. That struct carries `status`, `completion` and all five `qty_*` buckets — correctly, because the receive, damage and completion paths write them — and exposing it on the wire turned the generic CRUD update into a second, unguarded way to move a receipt. Measured against a live dev backend on 2026-07-31, on a receipt in `Closed`, a status whose `allowed_operations` list is EMPTY:

```text update_receipt_detail{ qty_received: 9999, status: "Open", completion: "Full" } → 200 OK ```

`qty_received` went 0 → 9999 against a `qty_expected` of 50, the line reopened inside a closed receipt, and the header was left reading `Closed / Pending` while its only line claimed `Full`. No version check, no stock movement, no audit row. `op1` (OPERATOR) could do it — while being denied `receipt_adjust_received_qty`, the command that does the same thing with an OCC version and a state-machine check.

The quantities are absent by CONSTRUCTION rather than filtered at runtime: a field that cannot be deserialized cannot be reintroduced by someone adding a line to a mapping function. They move only through their own commands.

Also absent, and each for its own reason: - `receipt_id` — re-parenting a line is not an edit, it is two lifecycle events on two receipts. - `container_id` — the supplier's expected LPN, fixed by the plan; the operator does not edit it. - `to_container_id` — where the stock physically is, set by receive. - `hold_code` — owned by put-on-hold / release. - `owner_id`, `receipt_type` — identity, fixed when the line is created. - `effective_date`, `uom_received` — stamped at receive time. `deny_unknown_fields` is the point, not a detail. Serde's default is to IGNORE fields it does not know, so a client sending `qty_received: 9999` would get `200 OK` and a response showing the old quantity — the write silently dropped, the caller convinced it landed. For a number the whole receipt is judged by, refusing loudly is the only honest answer.

manufactured_date.description: RF and web clients historically send different documented date dialects. `BusinessDate` preserves those dialects but rejects malformed input instead of silently turning it into an omitted update.

LotAttrCheckMode.description:
Per-line lot-attributes validation mode. Replaces the legacy pair of `match_lot_attributes: Option<bool>` (D-27) and `match_lot_attributes_strict: bool` (D-65 / ADR-050) with a single 3-state enum so the four-flag-combinations (one of which was a nonsensical `null + strict`) are no longer representable.

- `Disabled` — no validation; any scanned lot_attrs accepted as-is. Cascade tier 1 also stays lenient: an empty expected set on a candidate accumulates the operator's scan into that line. - `Advisory` — validation runs against expected lot_attrs; per-attribute supervisor overrides through `lot_policy_attribute.override_allowed` (D-27 / RPV code 36) are honoured. - `Strict` — ASN-pre-bound lot (pharma, EDI 856 contracts). `set_equal(expected, scanned)` is required. No overrides (RPV code 34, non-overridable).

DamageAction.description: Per Decisions Log D-26 + T-062 (migration 148). Action triggered by ReportDamage based on severity + OwnerConfig. The first three are the original on-report actions (just-record / hold-LPN / bump-qty-damaged). The four added in T-062 represent owner policy for auto-routing damage to a final disposition without manual intervention: * WriteOff  — auto-call WriteOffDamage on report (decrement inventory). * RTV       — auto-call MoveDamageToRtv on report (move to RTV staging). * Repurpose — flag disposition='Repurpose' (Phase 2 wires SKU substitute). * Destroy   — flag disposition='Destroyed' (Phase 3 wires regulated paths).

oneOf.description: Migration 160 — cosmetic damage (scratch / dent on the packaging); the goods are sold without a discount. Default action on this severity is `None` — the goods go into normal stock with an audit-record for statistics.

applied_action.description:
Migration 239 — the owner action that ACTUALLY ran when this row was written (`ReportDamage::handle_damage_action`).

Only `Reject` adds `damaged_qty` to `receipt_detail.qty_damaged`, so this is what tells a later reader which rows are echoed in that column and which are not — the distinction the line's damage ceiling stands on. Deriving it from today's `owner_config` instead would be wrong for history: the mapping is owner-configurable and can change between two reports on the same line.

`None` on a row created through plain CRUD (`create_receipt_detail_damage`): no action ran, nothing was echoed.

disposition.description: Final disposition decision. NULL = pending. Values: WrittenOff | RTV | Repurpose | Destroyed. VARCHAR (not enum) so Phase 2 vocabulary growth doesn't require ALTER TYPE.

move_failed.description: TRUE if auto-move to QC/Damage/RTV loc failed. Operator must resolve manually.

vendor_responsibility.description: Migration 161 — operator's assessment at receive: true = vendor is responsible for the damage (drives vendor-claim event in ERP); false (default) = warehouse-eaten / undecided. Audit-only — no Quark business logic branches on it; ERP integration consumes via outbox.

version.description: Per-row OCC version (Slice #3, migration 157). Independent of `receipt.version` (header) and `receipt_detail.version` (line). `receipt_set_damage_disposition` OCC-checks this on submit; `write_off_damage` / `move_damage_to_rtv` bump it without check (they're stateless terminal actions). Default 1 on insert.

schema.description: A [`DamageSeverity`] spelling. A `String` and not the enum on purpose: an unrecognised spelling must behave the way the SQL source behaved — match nothing tagged — and a typed field would have serde refuse the whole request instead.

DamageVocabularyItem.description: One thing the picker may offer.

code.description: What lands in the row and what the server compares — exactly, and case-sensitively.

display.description: What a human reads. Never sent back in place of [`Self::code`].

schema.description: Which of the two questions this answers.

stage.description: [`SEVERITY_STAGE`] | [`REASON_STAGE`]. A protocol token the client compares, not a word it prints.

schema.title: DamageVocabularyAnswer

methods.summary: What a damage report may say: with no severity, the four severities the `damage_severity` column accepts; with one, the `damage_reason` values tagged for it plus the untagged ones (`Other`). `stage` says which of the two was answered. A blank or unrecognised severity narrows rather than refusing — exactly as the metadata dropdown source it replaces did.

methods.name: receipt_damage_destination

schema.description:
What the destination field holds RIGHT NOW. Absent and empty mean the same thing, and both mean "nobody has put anything there yet".

The server cannot know this and must not guess it: it is the whole input to the rule that distinguishes a code the machine put there from a location the operator chose.

The severity the operator has picked, if any. A `String` for the same reason the vocabulary's is: an unrecognised spelling moves nothing and hides the field, which is what the transferred rule did with it — not a refusal of the whole request.
What the screen should do with its destination field.

prefill.description: The code to WRITE into the field. `None` means "leave what is there alone" — the operator chose it. `Some("")` is a real answer and not a missing one: the warehouse has no location of the needed type, and the field is cleared rather than filled with an invented fallback.

show.description: Draw the field at all. `false` for every severity that moves nothing.

schema.title: DamageDestination

methods.summary: Where a damage report of this severity sends the goods: whether the destination field is shown at all (only Major → QC and Total → Damage move anything), and the location code to put in it. `prefill` null means leave the operator's own choice alone; an empty string means the warehouse has no location of that type and the field is cleared rather than filled with a fallback. Send `current` — what the field holds now — or the answer cannot tell the operator's choice from a previous severity's prefill.

methods.name: receipt_damage_context

DamageContext.description: The line a damage report is about, and how much of it is still reportable.

already_damaged.description: Everything already reported damaged on this line, whatever each report then did to the line's own columns.

arrived.description: How much physically ARRIVED on this line — see [`LineQtyBuckets::arrived`]. Not `qty_received`.

receipt_no.description: The receipt's own number — what the operator calls the paperwork.

sku_descr.description: The SKU's description, as the owner's catalogue holds it.

uom.description: The line's unit of measure. Empty when the line names none.

methods.summary: What a damage report on one receipt line is about: the line number, the SKU and its description, the receipt number, the line's unit, how much physically ARRIVED on the line (not qty_received — a return booked as Damaged records its whole arrival in qty_damaged), how much has already been reported damaged, and how much may still be reported. The last number is the ceiling `receipt_report_damage` itself enforces, computed by the same function, so a client shows what the write will allow rather than guessing it. A line that does not exist answers null rather than refusing.

methods.name: receipt_damage_photo_upload_url

schema.description: Размер файла в байтах.
`Content-Type` файла. Он ПОДПИСЫВАЕТСЯ вместе со ссылкой, поэтому загрузчик обязан прислать ровно его — ответ повторяет его явно.

Запись о повреждении, если она уже существует (фотографию добавляют к сохранённому повреждению). Тогда потолок считается по уже сохранённым id этой записи. `None` — повреждение ещё не записано, и потолок сработает при сохранении: `receipt_report_damage` отказывает списку длиннее шести.

content_type.description: Тот `Content-Type`, который подписан. Пришлёте другой — подпись не сойдётся, и хранилище откажет.

expires_in_secs.description: Сколько секунд ссылка действительна. Не «до какого времени»: часы терминала и сервера расходятся, а разница длительностей — нет.

max_bytes.description: Предел на один файл, в байтах.

max_photos_per_record.description: Сколько фотографий держит одна запись о повреждении.

object_key.description: Ключ объекта. Его — и только его — клиент возвращает в `photo_attachment_ids`, когда сохраняет повреждение.

upload_url.description: Подписанная ссылка на `PUT`. Доверенность: в лог не писать, в состояние сессии не складывать.

methods.summary: Ask for a presigned PUT link to upload one damage photo, for a receipt line. Answers the object key to send back in receipt_report_damage's photo_attachment_ids, the link itself, the Content-Type that is SIGNED into it (send exactly that header or the signature will not match), and how many seconds the link lives. The server owns the limits and enforces them here and again on save: at most 6 photos per damage record (counted from the ids already stored — pass damage_record_id to have them counted), at most 10 MiB per file, and only image/jpeg, image/png, image/heic. A refusal says why in words. When the deployment has no object storage configured the answer is a refusal saying so — reporting the damage itself keeps working without photos, because photos are recommended and not required.

methods.name: receipt_damage_photo_view_urls

photos.description: В порядке, в котором ключи лежат в записи. Пусто — фотографий нет; это обычный ответ, а не отказ.

methods.summary: Presigned GET links for the photos already stored on one damage record. Keys come from the record itself, never from the caller, so a photo belonging to another receipt cannot be asked for. An empty list means the record has no photos — an ordinary answer, not a refusal. When the deployment has no object storage configured the answer is a refusal saying so; the damage record itself still reads normally through get_receipt_detail_damage.

methods.name: find_planned_case

case_label.description: Operator-scanned case label (= `container.code` of the case container). Filtered by receipt_id per D-69e SameReceipt scope.

PlannedCaseDetail.description: Detail projection for the case-level receive screens: the planned-case row joined with its parent line's SKU + owner and the pallet LPN. The case→line join lives here (model layer), so the RPC reads `find_planned_case` and `get_case_envelope` carry no SQL. Serialize + JsonSchema because it is returned on the wire by those Q-class endpoints.

owner_id.description: Owner the case's line belongs to (`receipt_detail.owner_id`).

pallet_lpn.description: Pallet LPN (`container.parent_id` → `code`); `None` when the case sits without a pallet.

methods.summary: Find a planned case row by label within a case-level receipt

methods.name: get_case_envelope

case_label.description: Operator-scanned case label (= `container.code` of the case container), resolved within this receipt per D-69e SameReceipt.

LotAttributePrompt.description: One operator-facing lot-attribute slot on a receive line screen, with the ASN-expected pre-fill and strict-lock resolved (ADR-050). Wire DTO — not a `lot_policy_attribute` row.

is_date.description:
`true` → this slot is a DATE, not free text: one of the four date columns `lot_policy` carries (`DATE_ATTRIBUTE_CODES`), folded in as a synthetic slot so RF and the web prompt for it alongside the custom attributes.

The server has always known this and never said it, so every renderer drew a text box and the operator typed a date into it by hand — `parse_date` then accepted or silently dropped whatever arrived. The flag does not change what is sent (still a string in `lot_attributes`); it lets a screen offer the right control for it.

readonly.description: `true` → operator may not edit. The line is strict-match (D-65) AND there is an expected value to enforce. Blank slots stay editable even on a strict line (nothing to lock).

value.description: ASN-expected value for this attribute on the scanned line, when the line carries one. `None` → blank input.

lot_policy_attributes.description: Lot-attribute prompt for the case's SKU (ADR-050): each shown attribute pre-filled with the line's ASN-expected value (`value`) and locked (`readonly`) when the line is strict-match. Empty when the SKU has no lot_policy. RF expands these into the RCCASE02LINE `_dyn_lot_attrs` widget so the operator confirms / supplies COLOR / dates / etc. before committing the case receive.

owner_id.description: Owner resolved from the parent `receipt_detail.owner_id` — RF copies it forward; the LINE call needs it on the wire.

sku_code.description: Parent SKU (from `receipt_detail.sku`) the scanned case belongs to.

methods.summary: Case envelope: resolve a scanned case label to its SKU + lot_policy_attributes for the RCCASE02LINE dynamic lot-attribute prompt

methods.name: validate_pallet_unique

pallet_lpn.description: LPN code the operator is about to assign (in CreateCaseLevelAsn, ReplacePallet's new_pallet_lpn, or any other pallet-create flow).

receipt_id.description: Optional: receipt the operator is working in. When supplied and the lpn exists on a DIFFERENT receipt the response flags it as a cross-receipt collision (the ReplacePallet command rejects this case at runtime; surfacing it in the validate response lets the UI prevent the operator from even submitting).

version.description:
OCC version (per CLAUDE.md classifier rules) — receipt is a stateful entity, downstream commands (`receipt_close` / `receipt_cancel` / `receipt_adjust_received_qty`) carry this on submit. RCASN01's `onResponseReceive.set` reads `response.version → display.receipt_version`; without it the rule silently resolved to undefined and any later stateful_command was sent without OCC protection.

The F2 picker (`lookup_asn`/`search_asns`) lists candidates only — the operator picks one and then the flow fetches details via `get_asn_by_number`. Exposing version on every picker row was the "version just in case from frontend" anti-pattern.

oneOf.description: Bare override code (receipt / dimensionless).

params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

schema.description: Operator scan against an already-loaded case-level receipt. Single scan = single RPC = single transaction (per OQ-05).

acknowledged_overrides.description: Override codes the operator already acknowledged via a prior `showConfirm` prompt — mirrors the same mechanism `receive_against_asn` uses. Empty on the first attempt; populated when re-submitted after a confirmation.

case_label.description: The case label the operator scanned. Resolves to `container.code` for a container row of `container_type='Case'` linked back to this receipt via `receipt_detail_case`.

lot_attributes.description: Operator-supplied lot attributes (COLOR, SIZE, etc.) from the RCCASE02 `_dyn_lot_attrs` capture. Merged over the line's ASN-expected snapshot in `deposit_for_case_scan`: operator value wins on conflict and fills attributes the ASN did not pre-declare. Empty → the planning/expected snapshot is used unchanged (prior behaviour). Applies to BOTH planned and unplanned paths.

override_grant_id.description: A supervisor's grant (`supervisor_override_grant`) authorising a capability-gated override of a planned case's count — a per-case shortage (28) or excess (27) — for an operator who does not hold the capability. Its pairs must name the receipt LINE the case belongs to: `{code, subject: "receipt:<receipt_id>/line:<receipt_detail_id>"}` (the case's parent `receipt_detail`, not the case itself); a refused scan names that exact pair in `context.pairs`. The authoriser recorded is the grant's, never a field of this request. Optional: a caller who holds the capability keeps acknowledging with the bare code in `acknowledged_overrides`, exactly as before. See `shared::override_grant`.

qty.description: Physically-counted qty. Usually matches the planned `receipt_detail_case.expected_qty` but short / over receipts are allowed at the line level (rolled into the parent `receipt_detail.qty_received` and surfaced via the existing excess/shortage `AllowError` policy chain at receipt close).

sku_code.description: Optional SKU code. Required when sub-chunk 2 lands the unplanned-case path (we need to know the SKU before the policy check can decide whether to auto-create a parent receipt_detail). In sub-chunk 1's happy path it's unused — the planned case row resolves SKU through receipt_detail_id.

to_loc.description: Physical landing location for the scanned case (the dock/door or the put-away staging zone, whichever the warehouse uses for at-receive-time storage).

uom_received.description: Unit the operator used to enter `qty`. Drives the case-vs-EA translation done inside this command: * `Some("CS")` — "I received N cases" (RF default in the widget). For a planned case the backend multiplies by that case's expected quantity; for an unplanned case it uses the receipt line's active pack hierarchy. qty=1 with planned 10 EA/case → 10 EA deposit. The full-case path is the trusted-label scenario; receipt_policy validation still runs in case the operator typed a partial case (qty=0.5 CS = 5 EA on a 10-pack). * `Some("EA")` — "I opened the case and physically counted N units". qty IS the base-UOM total. Backend compares against the planned case qty and routes any deviation through `receipt_policy.{shortage,excess}_*` rules so the operator either gets a clean override prompt (within allowed %) or a hard rejection. * `None` — back-compat default = treat qty as base-UOM (EA). Pre-widget clients (integration tests, older RF builds) send qty in EA directly without specifying uom.

container_id.description: `container.id` of the case container — useful for follow-up label-print or move operations.

line_complete.description: True when the just-scanned case rolled the line up to `qty_received >= qty_expected`. RCCASE02 branches on this to auto-navigate to RCCASE_DONE (close confirmation) instead of leaving the operator stuck on the scan loop with no more planned cases to receive.

line_qty_received.description: Receipt-detail line `qty_received` after this scan rolled forward — lets the RF UI show "23 of 50 received" without an extra round-trip.

receipt_detail_case_id.description: Primary key of the `receipt_detail_case` row that flipped to Received (or was synthesised, in sub-chunks 2-3).

was_unplanned.description: True when the row was synthesised under the `unplanned_case_on_asn = Allow | Warning` path. Sub-chunk 1 always returns false (synthesis lands in sub-chunk 2).

schema.description: `Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`, for the reason [`super::PutawayStepCriterion`] gives: the step editor's sentence is rendered by `web-ui-server`, which reads the step back over `get_putaway_policy_detail` and needs the four axis enums and the six booleans as TYPES, not as strings it re-parses.

allow_mixed_sku.description:
Whether the suggested location may already hold other SKUs / other lots, and whether it must be empty.

`Some(true)` / `Some(true)` / `Some(false)` is the state a step is in when it says nothing about mixing: the location's own flags and the commingle rules decide. That is what `INHERIT` meant, and it is the column default — a step that says nothing about mixing must not start forbidding it.

**`None` used to be that state too, and app migration 290 removed it.** `MixCheck::from_toggles` (`wms-inventory`) reads `None` and `Some(true)` on a mixing toggle into the SAME arm, so the two were already indistinguishable to the engine while the step card drew `None` as an UNTICKED box — which reads as "mixing is not allowed", the opposite of what the engine did. Filling the NULLs is what makes the box tell the truth. The columns stay nullable (nothing writes NULL today, and NOT NULL is its own decision), so this type keeps its `Option` and every reader here keeps reading three values.

fit_by_cube.description:
Which PHYSICAL checks this step applies (migration 231).

`NOT NULL`, unlike the three mixing toggles above: those need a third "no opinion" state because the location's own flags can answer instead, and these have nothing to defer to. `fit_by_cube` / `fit_by_weight` default `true` because that is what the engine has always done; `fit_by_pallet_dims` defaults `false` because it is new arithmetic.

Read as a set by [`crate::model::policies`]' consumer `putaway::space::FitToggles`, never one at a time — the whole point of three columns is that they are independent, and a caller that reads one of them alone is deciding for the other two.

fit_by_quantity.description: What the location already holds, plus what is arriving, against `location.max_qty_capacity` — how a pick face is sized: it holds so many EACHes and then it is full.

fit_by_stack_limit.description: Refuse a location whose pallet POSITIONS are taken — `location.footprint × location.stack_limit`, the count Infor calls Fit by Stack Limit. The one capacity a bulk floor bay actually has, and the only one that binds in a warehouse keeping no cube on its items.

respect_temperature.description: Reject a location whose temperature range does not cover the SKU's. The numbers come from the SKU card, never retyped here, so the step cannot drift away from the product master.

sequence.description: Execution order within the policy. Unique per policy (migration 191).

step_num.description: User-facing step label. NOT an ordering key — see `sequence`.

version.description: Optimistic lock (migration 349). Absent from `PutawayPolicyDetailForUpdate` — a caller must never write it; it moves only through [`PutawayPolicyDetailBmc::update_checked`], which bumps it in the same statement as the write.
