oneOf.description: Is the pallet a full pallet of its pack, or a part of one (`SPEC_putaway_assigned_slot.md` §5)? A `Product` property: it decides whether the step applies to the pallet.
The row narrows what the STEP APPLIES TO — the incoming pallet.
The row narrows the candidate locations.

schema.description: `Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`, unlike most entities here: the step editor's sentence (`putaway_step_describe`) is rendered by `web-ui-server`, which has no database of its own and reads a step's criteria back over `list_putaway_step_criterion`. Reading them into the entity — rather than picking fields out of a `serde_json::Value` on the web side — is what keeps `describe_step`'s exhaustive matches meaningful: a hand-parsed row could carry a property spelling no `CriterionProperty` variant has, and the compiler would never notice.

attribute_code.description: Which attribute the criterion narrows on (COLOR, SIZE) — set for exactly the three attribute properties (`LotAttribute`, `SkuAttribute`, `LocationAttribute`) and NULL for every other. `chk_step_criterion_attribute_code` (migration 209, widened by 218) enforces the pairing in both directions.

values.description:
The `text[]` column (migration 209): one column serves every property kind (an enum's SQL label, `'true'`/`'false'`, or a one-element array for a scalar) because the resolver — not the storage — knows the type.

A plain `Vec<String>`, carried by `Fields` like every other column: the workspace enables the `postgres-array` feature on both `sea-query` and `sea-query-binder`, so `Vec<String>` converts into a `sea_query::Value::Array` and binds as a real `text[]`. No cast-as is needed (the column is `text[]`, not an enum array), and no newtype — this field was `#[field(skip)]` until that feature was turned on, which is also why `putaway_policy_detail.rs` once wrapped its `loc_type[]` columns in a local `LocTypes` newtype with five hand-written trait impls. Both workarounds are gone; the whole entity now travels the generic CRUD path.

**An empty array is not NULL, and is not a state a row can be in.** `chk_step_criterion_values_nonempty` (migration 209) rejects `cardinality(values) = 0` at this table, so "no values" is a write-time database refusal rather than something stored and later interpreted — a reader here never has to decide what an empty criterion means. (It would mean "narrow the candidates to nothing", indistinguishable in a trace from an exhausted zone. That is the refusal's whole point.)

PutawayStepCriterion.description: `Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`, unlike most entities here: the step editor's sentence (`putaway_step_describe`) is rendered by `web-ui-server`, which has no database of its own and reads a step's criteria back over `list_putaway_step_criterion`. Reading them into the entity — rather than picking fields out of a `serde_json::Value` on the web side — is what keeps `describe_step`'s exhaustive matches meaningful: a hand-parsed row could carry a property spelling no `CriterionProperty` variant has, and the compiler would never notice.

attribute_code.description: Which attribute the criterion narrows on (COLOR, SIZE) — set for exactly the three attribute properties (`LotAttribute`, `SkuAttribute`, `LocationAttribute`) and NULL for every other. `chk_step_criterion_attribute_code` (migration 209, widened by 218) enforces the pairing in both directions.

values.description:
The `text[]` column (migration 209): one column serves every property kind (an enum's SQL label, `'true'`/`'false'`, or a one-element array for a scalar) because the resolver — not the storage — knows the type.

A plain `Vec<String>`, carried by `Fields` like every other column: the workspace enables the `postgres-array` feature on both `sea-query` and `sea-query-binder`, so `Vec<String>` converts into a `sea_query::Value::Array` and binds as a real `text[]`. No cast-as is needed (the column is `text[]`, not an enum array), and no newtype — this field was `#[field(skip)]` until that feature was turned on, which is also why `putaway_policy_detail.rs` once wrapped its `loc_type[]` columns in a local `LocTypes` newtype with five hand-written trait impls. Both workarounds are gone; the whole entity now travels the generic CRUD path.

**An empty array is not NULL, and is not a state a row can be in.** `chk_step_criterion_values_nonempty` (migration 209) rejects `cardinality(values) = 0` at this table, so "no values" is a write-time database refusal rather than something stored and later interpreted — a reader here never has to decide what an empty criterion means. (It would mean "narrow the candidates to nothing", indistinguishable in a trace from an exhausted zone. That is the refusal's whole point.)

PutawayPipelineStep.description: One step of the pipeline: its fields, its conditions, its words, and every verdict about it.

clauses.description: The running sentence, in the pieces the card's three bands need (`narrate_step`'s own topics, not this file's).

criteria.description: The step's conditions, in the order `list_for_step` returns them — the `property` enum's own declaration order.

never_runs_after.description: The `step_num` of the earlier step that leaves this one nothing to place, when there is one. A `step_num` and not an id: it is what the operator reads on the card.

refusals.description: Why this step, AS THE OPERATOR IS HOLDING IT, cannot be saved. Always empty for a stored step — see the module doc.

version.description: This step's own optimistic lock — per step, never per policy, because two supervisors editing two different steps must not collide.

oneOf.description: Candidate zone named on the step itself (`to_zone`).
Candidate zone taken from the SKU's putaway zone.
Single candidate location named on the step (`to_location`).

PutawayStepFields.description:
The seventeen card fields, under their own column names.

Spelled out rather than embedding [`PutawayPolicyDetail`] whole: the card edits exactly these, and a wire shape that also carried `add_who` / `mod_when` / `putaway_policy_id` would invite a draft to send them back.

allow_mixed_sku.description: `None` is a meaning of its own — "this step has no opinion about what the location may already hold" — and not an absence. These three and the four anchors above are the columns a save may set back to NULL by sending an explicit `null` (`PUTAWAY_STEP_CLEARABLE_COLUMNS`); a null on any other field of the card is ignored, as it always was.

fit_by_cube.description: All FIVE fit toggles. The mockup draws three; migration 447 added `fit_by_stack_limit` and `fit_by_quantity` after it was drawn, and a card that showed three would remove a capability the current screen already has.

Run.description: The clause's words, cut into the values the operator chose and the rest. Concatenated, `text` of every run is the clause's own `text`, byte for byte.

bold.description: A value the operator picked — the card sets these in bold.

missing.description:
Words standing where a value the step NEEDS is not set — the card draws these amber, in place.

A FLAG and not a marker to match, because the marker is a translated phrase: the card used to be expected to find the gap by looking for its words in the clause, which needed the words sent to it, and nothing ever sent them. Never `true` together with `bold`.

policy_version.description: The policy's own optimistic lock — what a reorder must echo back.

steps.description: Every step of the policy in execution order (`sequence`, never `step_num` — that is `varchar(5)` and sorts '10' before '2').

DryRunCandidate.description: One predicate's verdict on one candidate location.

detail.description: What that outcome said: the measurement that refused, its limit, what was attempted. `None` for a pass.

outcome.description: `offered`, or `refused (<code>)` — worded here so the panel never parses a rejection code.

DryRunOutcome.description:
How one step of the pipeline answered.

An enum and not a string: the panel styles these four differently and a string would make that styling a client-side parse of engine vocabulary — the one thing this whole module exists to stop.

oneOf.description: This step offered the location the engine took.
This step ran its candidate scan and reserved nothing.
This step was not about this pallet, or had nowhere to look.
The engine returned before this step: an earlier one matched, or the walk stopped. No trace entry exists for it at all.

container_id.description: What the engine was actually asked about — `container.id`, which is what `explain_location` takes.

location.description: Where the pallet is standing now.

note.description:
Anything that needs saying about the LIST rather than about the pallet — today, the two ways [`lines`](Self::lines) can hold fewer rows than the LPN's stock did: it was cut at [`PALLET_LINES_CAP`], or rows under this LPN sit on a different container and are not on this pallet.

Not in the plan's interface sketch. It is here because a supervisor counting a short list must never have to wonder which of those happened — a report that quietly showed 200 of 201 lines, or half a pallet, would be the one thing this module is built not to do.

DryRunPalletLine.description: One SKU line on the pallet.

DryRunStep.description: One step of the pipeline, as the dry run found it.

candidates.description: Only for the step that MATCHED. Every other step's candidate list is the story of a scan that led nowhere, and a panel drawing all of them would bury the one that answered.

explanation.description: The outcome in words, including the pipeline position, so one line of the report reads on its own.

searched_location.description: The single location this step searched, when its scope named one.

step_num.description: The step's own `step_num`, exactly as the policy stores it — the panel matches its cards on this.

zone.description: The zone this step searched. For a `Location` scope this is the zone the searched LOCATION sits in, not the space that was searched — read [`Self::searched_location`] first.

schema.description: What the engine would do with one LPN under one policy, in words.

chosen.description: The location the engine would take, when a step matched.

lpn.description: Echoed back, trimmed — the panel keeps its own field, and a report that did not name its subject cannot be read beside a second one.

pallet.description: What the LPN carries. `None` when the report was refused before a pallet was known, and present even for some refusals: knowing WHAT is on the pallet is most of the answer to "why did nothing match it".

refusal.description: Why there is no walk to report, worded. Not an error: an operator who typed an unknown LPN asked a question and gets an answer.

steps.description: EVERY step of the policy, in `sequence` order. Empty only when the report was refused.

verdict.description: One sentence: which step won, or that none did. Always present, so the panel has exactly one thing to print at the top — on a refusal it is the refusal, said once rather than in two places that could disagree.

schema.title: PutawayDryRun

methods.summary: What the putaway engine would do with one LPN under one policy, in words: the pallet, which step wins and where it would go, and every step of the pipeline with why it did or did not answer — including the ones the engine never reached. Evaluates the SAVED policy, not an unsaved draft, so a step edited on screen is previewed only after it is saved. Reserves nothing (the walk is rolled back). An LPN carrying no stock, or loose stock rather than a container, comes back as a worded `refusal` on a successful response — not as an error; only a policy that does not exist or will not load is a refusal of the call.

block_inbound_flow.description:
Does this hold forbid PUTTING stock into the place it covers?

Separate from [`Self::block_outbound_flow`] because the warehouse asks two different questions of one hold, and one flag used to answer both. The dedicated damage bay carries a permanent `Damaged` hold so its contents never reach an order — that is a PICKING ban — and the same flag was read as "nothing may be put here", which refused the damaged return the bay exists to receive. `enforce` / `overridable` stay the STRENGTH of the ban; these two say what it applies TO.

block_outbound_flow.description:
Does this hold forbid TAKING stock out of the place it covers?

Read by the availability view (`inventory_balance_atp`), by the reservation re-check (`InventoryHoldBmc::covers_position`) and by the source side of a move. See [`Self::block_inbound_flow`].

rank.description:
Intended as the dropdown sort order (low rank on top, migration 142).

**Nothing reads it.** It did NOT set loc_status precedence, whatever this comment claimed before: `derive_loc_status` (`wms-inventory::hold`) ranks a location by matching the literal code `"Damaged"`, so renumbering ranks changes no behaviour — and the admin form (migration 189) nevertheless demands a value for it. Kept as-is rather than dropped because that is the owner's call, not a cleanup: see migration 199, which dropped `ack_code` for exactly this reason once the same question was answered.

params.name: meta

oneOf.description: Bare override code (receipt / dimensionless).
Move override pair (dimension code + hold-code subject).

params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

MoveContext.description:
Input contract for `MoveCommand`. Caller fills exactly one source pattern (container_id / lpn / loc), exactly one destination pattern, and optional qty (None = full move; Some = partial — only valid when `source_type.allows_partial_qty()`).

Per ADR-055 §D-9: MoveCommand is a dumb primitive — it does NOT resolve destinations from `owner_config.default_*_loc` or any allocation policy. Caller is responsible for providing the final `dest_loc` / `dest_lpn` / `dest_container_id` ready-to-use. `deny_unknown_fields` is load-bearing, not tidiness (F6).

This struct just LOST `acknowledged_overrides` and `authorized_by`. Serde's default is to ignore fields it does not know, so a client still sending them would have its acknowledgement silently dropped: the supervisor types a password, the ack goes nowhere, the move refuses again, and nothing anywhere says why. That is the precise failure mode this whole feature exists to remove — an authorization that looks accepted and is not.

With this, a client that has not adopted `override_grant_id` fails loudly at the parse, naming the field it should not be sending.

dest_lpn_auto.description: When `true` and no `dest_lpn`/`dest_container_id` is given, the primitive GENERATES a fresh LPN (`ContainerService::generate_container_code`) and lands the stock in that NEW container at `dest_loc`, instead of landing loose. The caller (Hard-Move "New → Auto") sets this; the primitive stays dumb — it just resolves "a new container, you pick the code". Ignored when `dest_lpn` is set (that names the container) or the dest location is `discard_lpn` (which forces loose).

idempotency_key.description:
The move's idempotency key.

Required by every layer below the RPC boundary — `transaction_log` rows and the idempotency store both assume it is real. On the WIRE it may be omitted, because a client whose key is derived from the payload hash (rf-go, `submit_state.go:78`) cannot put the key inside the payload without circularity; such clients send it in the ADR-058 `meta` envelope instead, and `move_execute` fills it in before the pipeline runs. A context still holding [`IdempotencyKey::unset`] past the boundary is a bug the boundary is required to have rejected.

The default is NAMED on purpose: bare `#[serde(default)]` would invent a fresh random key (that is what `Default` for this type does), so an omitted key would silently become a real one and its retry would double-execute rather than dedupe.

override_grant_id.description:
The server-minted grant authorizing this move's overrides (`supervisor_override_grant`, F6). The acknowledged pairs AND the authorizer are read from that row — neither is a field the client can assert, which is the whole of F6: before it, an operator could post `acknowledged_overrides` + any `authorized_by` and move stock off a held pallet, and `transaction_log` recorded the forged authorizer.

`None` for the overwhelming majority of moves, which need no override at all — that case must stay the cheap one, with no extra round trip.

pending_move_in_id.description:
The reservation (`inventory_pending_move_in.id`) the putaway engine took when it chose this location. Set ONLY when the SYSTEM directed the move — it switches the primitive into directed mode, where a landing conflict on the directed location resolves as an acknowledgeable deviation or a redirect instead of a bare refusal, and where a successful move retires the reservation.

It is a HANDLE, never a promise: `putaway_suggest_location` is idempotent for days while a reservation lives for minutes, so a replayed response can carry an id whose reservation has already expired. The executor re-reads the row (`movement::directed::open`) and refuses a stale one rather than trusting the caller.

qty.description: `None` = full move; `Some(n)` = partial. Only valid when `source_type.allows_partial_qty()` returns `true`.

reason_code.description: Free-form audit hint, ≤80 chars (mirrors `transaction_log.reason_code` VARCHAR(80) constraint per migration 144).

recursive.description: Subtree move (existing `MoveContainer.recursive` flag): when `true`, child containers move with the root.

serial_numbers.description: Operator-scanned unit serials for a serial-tracked PARTIAL move — the specific units to move, from the RF terminal. `None`/empty for a full move (all serials follow the qty) or for non-serial stock. The primitive never chooses which serials move, so a partial move of serial-tracked stock must name them.

oneOf.description:
Audit discriminator ONLY — `transaction_log.source_type = "pick"` and the validation-matrix row for an outbound-style move of FREE stock.

It is **not** the Pick operation and **never** proof of a right to consume reserved stock: a Generic Move with this source type still runs in `AvailableMove` accounting, refuses `qty_allocated` / `qty_picked` like every other move, and never touches a `pick_detail`, its reservation or its task. Executing a Pick is `picking::execute_reserved_pick` (the stock-move kernel's `ReservedPick` accounting, entered only after the pick is proved under lock) — never `MovementService::execute` with this variant, and never "release the reservation, then Move".

The wire value `"pick"` is kept as is; changing it needs its own compatibility decision (stock-move-kernel debt, slice 5).

already_printed_lpn.description: F2(b): the LPN the operator already printed by hand for this move (the New-LPN "Print" button fires before submit so the label can be applied to the pallet). When it equals the container the move creates, `move_execute` skips the post-commit auto-print — otherwise the pallet gets two identical labels. Optional + defaulted so every non-New-LPN caller omits it and the pipeline (which reads only `ctx`) is unaffected.

InventoryStatusHold.description:
Mirror of the PostgreSQL `inv_hold_code` enum (15 values after migration 142).

Migration 142 renamed and extended the DB enum: - `QCRec` → `QcQuarantine` (semantic clarity: not just "at receive") - `Return` → `CustomerReturn` (disambiguate from `Rtv`) - Added: `Rtv`, `Destroy`, `QcRequired`, `NewItem`, `NotHold`

oneOf.description: Administrative location block — hard, non-overridable. Carries the legacy `location.status='Hold'` block preserved by migration 194 (F8). A varchar-only `inventory_hold.code` value; it is never written to the `inv_hold_code` DB enum column (`inventory_hold.status`), so it needs no DB-enum `ALTER`.
Code 80 acknowledged: source LPN had active hold, override applied.
Code 81 acknowledged: source location had `loc_flag != None`, override applied.
Code 82 acknowledged: destination location had `loc_flag != None`, override applied.

Code 85 acknowledged: the SYSTEM directed this location, a soft rule refused it, and the operator confirmed the placement anyway.

`subject` is the rule that was overruled (`capacity`, `sku_mixing`, …) — the OTHER half of the `(code, subject)` ack pair the operator actually authorized, so the audit record names the same thing the prompt did. `detail` is the refusal in full (which SKU, which limit), which neither the code nor the subject can carry.

The directed move landed, but its reservation was no longer `Active` by the time the executor retired it — the TTL sweeper or a re-suggest got there first. Not a failure (the stock did arrive), but it means the location was released and possibly re-promised while the operator was walking, so it is surfaced rather than swallowed.

schema.description:
Success-path return. Failures surface via `MoveError`.

Completion timestamp deliberately NOT included — the outbox event `inventory.moved` carries the canonical timestamp, and `transaction_log` has `add_when` per move line. Adding it here would only duplicate.

ask_location_empty.description: Count spec Appendix L (ZERO_CONFIRMATION): the move took the last stock out of `source_location`, and the moved stock's owner asks (`owner_config.confirm_empty_on_move`) — the RF asks the operator whether that location is empty (`location_confirm_empty`, source `Move`, `source_id` = `move_log_id`). Only a manual move asks.

created_lpn.description: The LPN of a container this move CREATED (New-LPN: manual or auto), so the caller can auto-print its label. `None` when the move relocated, merged into an existing container, or landed loose — nothing new to label.

move_log_id.description: The move's first `transaction_log` row: the operation an answer names.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings (e.g. `acknowledged_overrides` consumed; future a warning for a hold that does not move with the stock, once Phase 3 lands `inventory_hold.moves_with_stock`).

schema.title: MoveResult

methods.summary: Generic Move primitive — validates and executes inventory movement (Putaway, Pick, MoveToQc, MoveToDamage, MoveToRtv, ReleaseFromQc, etc.) with full pipeline. Pass pending_move_in_id (from putaway_suggest_location) to run the move as DIRECTED: the executor re-validates that reservation, downgrades a soft rule broken on the reserved location to an acknowledgement instead of a refusal, answers a process-banned location with a redirect, and retires the reservation when the stock lands. An acknowledgement is a PAIR, {code, subject}, sent back in meta.acknowledged_overrides: for a directed deviation the code is 85 and the subject is the rule that refused (capacity, sku_mixing, lot_mixing, multi_lot_on_lpn, attribute_mixing, loc_type) — ONE pair per rule, never per offending line. Every unacknowledged pair of the whole move arrives together in error.data.detail.context.pairs with is_overridable=true, so one prompt collects them all; acking a pair the server did not raise is a hard UnknownAckSubject, not silent leniency. A redirect answers with error.data.detail.context.redirect = {location, pending_move_in_id} — the nearest usable location to the one being refused, ALREADY RESERVED for this pallet (pass that id back as pending_move_in_id to stay in directed mode), with the promise on the refused location released; when no replacement could be named there is no context and the client asks putaway_suggest_location again. Directed leniency applies ONLY while dest_loc is the reserved location — a destination the operator chose themselves keeps every ordinary refusal. A move out of or into a location an open Hard inventory count is counting is refused (LOCATION_BEING_COUNTED, is_overridable=true); context.pairs names the pair {code: 87, subject: "count:<inventory_count_id>"} a shift lead's supervisor_override_grant must carry — with a reason, which is recorded on the count — and its id goes in ctx.override_grant_id like every other move override.

schema.title: SuggestLocation

schema.description:
The suggestion as it goes over the wire.

`location: None` with a `reason` is a normal answer — the warehouse had nothing to offer — not an error. An error means the engine could not ASK the question.

# One idempotency key per user intent — every re-ask needs a fresh one

A `null` location IS a success, so the runner stores it and replays it for the key's whole TTL (days). The natural retry after [`REASON_PALLET_ALREADY_RESERVED`] — same pallet, nothing new to exclude — is a byte-identical payload, so re-using the key does not re-ask the engine: it replays the stale "no" even though that reason is documented as retryable. `exclude_locations` changes the hash and so re-asks on its own, but a plain retry does not.

So: mint a NEW `idempotency_key` for every re-ask. The key deduplicates ONE user intent ("where does this pallet go, asked now") against network retries of that same request; a second ask is a second intent.

expires_at.description:
RFC3339. When it lapses the reservation stops holding space; the operator has to ask again.

**A replayed value may already be in the past.** The idempotency TTL is days and a reservation's is minutes, so a late retry on the same key replays a `pending_move_in_id` whose reservation has since expired. Shortening the shared idempotency TTL for this one command would trade a general contract for a special case, so the id is deliberately not a guarantee: whoever executes against it re-checks the row is still `status = Active AND expires_at > now()` rather than trusting the handle. `move_execute` does exactly that (`movement::directed::open`) and answers a stale handle with `ReservationNotUsable` — the client's cue to ask for a fresh suggestion under a fresh idempotency key.

pending_move_in_id.description:
Hand this to `move_execute` as `pending_move_in_id` to run the suggestion as a DIRECTED move: the executor then treats a soft rule broken on this location as an acknowledgeable deviation rather than a refusal, and retires the reservation when the pallet lands.

Not a guarantee: see [`Self::expires_at`]. The executor re-reads the row and refuses a stale handle outright rather than silently running an undirected move.

reason.description: Set exactly when `location` is `None`. One of [`REASON_PALLET_ALREADY_RESERVED`] / [`REASON_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOCATION`] — a code and not a sentence, because the caller branches on it (retry vs. escalate) and the operator-facing wording is the client's to choose.

trace.description: [`PutawayTrace`], as JSON. Present on success too — there it is the record of which step won and what it passed over.

schema.title: SuggestLocationResult

methods.summary: Suggest and reserve the location a received LPN should be put away into. Reserves space in inventory_pending_move_in and returns pending_move_in_id — pass it to move_execute as pending_move_in_id to run the move as DIRECTED: a soft rule broken on that location (capacity, mixing, loc_type) then asks the operator to acknowledge the pair {code:85, subject:<the rule that refused>} instead of refusing, a process ban on the location answers with a redirect, and the reservation is retired when the pallet lands. A null location with a reason means nothing qualified — read trace for which rule refused how many locations. Mint a FRESH idempotency_key for every re-ask: a null answer is a success, so re-using the key replays that null for the key's whole TTL instead of asking again; one key per user intent. A replayed expires_at may already be in the past — the reservation TTL is minutes, the idempotency TTL days — so the id is a handle, not a promise: move_execute re-checks the row is still Active and unexpired and refuses a stale one outright rather than quietly running an undirected move.

The answer, over the wire — and deliberately NOT [`SuggestLocationResult`].

That struct carries `pending_move_in_id` and `expires_at`: handles to a row this call's transaction never commits. Shipping them here would hand a client an id that names nothing the moment the response leaves the process — worse than omitting it, because a caller could mistake it for something `move_execute` might accept. `location`, `reason` and `trace` are facts about the DECISION the engine reached, which the rollback does not erase; nothing on this struct is a handle to a database row.

The response carries location, reason and trace — the same fields putaway_suggest_location returns for those — but never pending_move_in_id or expires_at: this call reserves nothing, so there is no row for either to name. Built for the putaway step page's dry-run panel; any caller wanting to preview a policy without disturbing a live pallet is the intended audience.

methods.summary: Release a pending putaway reservation, freeing the location before its TTL expires. Cancels the inventory_pending_move_in row named by id, together with any neighbour positions it shares a reservation group with (an oversized load spanning several positions holds one row per position) — the whole group releases as one call. The location's promised space (active_totals) drops by the released rows' cube and weight immediately, so the next putaway_suggest_location can offer the location again. A multi-position group is tied together by `share_of`.

oneOf.description: Held by the directed-putaway engine for a suggested location.
Held by replenishment for the pick face it is topping up.
Held by an operator-driven move.
Holding space. The ONLY status that counts toward promised space.

The stock arrived — the space is now real occupancy in `inventory_balances`, so this row must stop counting or the location is charged twice. That is literal on the ANCHOR row: the load landed in exactly that location. A NEIGHBOUR row (`share_of` set) never receives stock itself — `retire_group` still stamps it `Consumed`, one status for the whole group rather than the group disagreeing about one event — and there it means the promise ended because the load it was holding a position FOR has arrived; from that moment the position is held by the section holds landing places (`putaway::section_holds`), not by this reservation any more.
The suggestion was withdrawn (re-suggest, operator refusal).
The TTL ran out before the stock arrived; the sweeper flipped it.

schema.description:
Represents a hold placed on inventory, supporting lot, location, or LPN-based holds.

This struct is designed for detailed tracking and auditing of inventory holds in a warehouse management system. It supports flexible hold types (lot, location, LPN), status management, and full audit trails.

# Fields - `id`: Unique identifier for the hold record. - `code`: Business code for the hold (may be used for grouping or referencing). - `lot`: Optional lot number, if the hold is placed at the lot level. - `loc`: Optional location code, if the hold is placed at the location level. - `lpn`: Optional License Plate Number, if the hold is placed on a movable unit. - `is_hold_on`: `true` if the hold is currently active, `false` if released. - `status`: The current status of the hold (custom enum). - `date_on`: Timestamp when the hold was placed. - `who_on`: User ID or actor who placed the hold. - `date_off`: Timestamp when the hold was released (if applicable). - `who_off`: User ID or actor who released the hold (if applicable). - `comments`: Optional comments or notes about the hold. - `hours_to_hold`: Optional planned duration (in hours) for the hold. - `auto_release_date`: Optional date when the hold should be automatically released. - `add_who`: User ID who created the record. - `add_when`: Timestamp when the record was created. - `mod_who`: User ID who last modified the record. - `mod_when`: Timestamp when the record was last modified.

# Serialization - Uses RFC3339 datetime format for all timestamps. - Designed for use with Serde and SQLx for seamless database and API integration.

# Example ``` let hold = InventoryHold { id: 1, code: "HOLD-2025-001".to_string(), lot: Some("LOT-123".to_string()), loc: None, lpn: None, is_hold_on: true, status: InventoryStatusHold::Active, date_on: OffsetDateTime::now_utc(), who_on: 42, date_off: OffsetDateTime::now_utc(), who_off: 0, comments: Some("Quality check pending".to_string()), hours_to_hold: Some(24.0), auto_release_date: OffsetDateTime::now_utc(), add_who: 42, add_when: OffsetDateTime::now_utc(), mod_who: 42, mod_when: OffsetDateTime::now_utc(), }; ```

business_operation.description: Polymorphic discriminator (spec §7.4 / §16.8). Drives both the open-context extractor and the commit dispatcher. Defaults to `Receive` so callers from the existing receipt flow don't need to be updated.

business_ref_id.description: Polymorphic reference to the business document the episode is anchored to: * Receive  → `receipt_detail.id` * Move     → `move.id` * Pick     → `pick_task.id` (line via `business_ref_line`) * Pack     → `shipping_carton.id` * Ship     → `shipment.id` * Return   → `receipt.id` (RMA) * Adjust   → `inventory_adjustment.id` * Inventory→ `count_session.id`

serial_number.description: The serial barcode the operator just scanned.

to_location.description:
Receive-context location. Required on the FIRST `Receive` call (no open episode yet); ignored on subsequent. Server stores on the episode and reuses at commit time.

Client doesn't have a numeric container_id anyway, only the LPN string operators typed at receive-time, which the receive handler already resolved into the FK before we get here.

already_captured.description: `true` when `serial_number` was already in this episode — the insert was a no-op and the counter did NOT increment. UI uses it to surface the spec §10.1 "accidentally scanned twice? Y/N" prompt.

EpisodeForceCloseRow.description:
Denormalised row returned by [`SerialCaptureEpisodeBmc::list_force_close_candidates_for_warehouse`]. Sibling of [`OperatorOpenEpisodeRow`] tailored for the supervisor force-close screen (slice B):

- Adds `operator_id` so the supervisor knows whose episode they're about to terminate. - Status filter is broader — also includes `Abandoned` (TTL- terminated, needs supervisor decision per slice 3f). - No operator filter — supervisor sees every blocking episode in the warehouse, not just their own.

- Covers Receive AND Pick episodes. An Abandoned Pick episode blocks moves of its stock through the movement service (`move_execute`; ADR-090 `EpisodeMoveGuard`) until a supervisor resolves it, so the supervisor must be able to find it here.

Display fields are joined in, so the picker renders without N+1 lookups.

Pre-enriched with business_operation, document_number (receipt or order number), location, owner and operator_id for the RCSN_FORCE picker label (slice B).

oneOf.description: Vendor pre-advised in ASN.
Operator scanned at receive.
Pre-applied by manufacturer (Phase 5+).
Manually entered by admin.

**Exists for DB compatibility only.** `serial_status` has had this label since the serial spec's phase 1 (`PackSerial`, `Picked → Packed → Shipped`), but the command and its transitions never landed. Without the variant a row carrying it would not decode, and every `SELECT *` over `inventory_balances_serial` would fail.

Packing MUST NOT write this status: the FSM has no transition into or out of it, and `contract-tests::packed_serial_status` keeps every other file from naming it. A packed serial's place is its container (post-pick spec D-51); serial-aware packing is a later decision.
A count expected it here and did not find it (count spec Appendix K): not in the warehouse, no location. A later count that finds it brings it back to `Active`.

received_via.description: `receipt_detail.id` of the line that captured it; `None` for a serial a count registered (`registered_via_count`).

registered_via_adjustment.description: The adjustment that registered one (adjustment spec Appendix D).

registered_via_count.description: The count task that registered a serial no receipt brought (count spec Appendix K).

Строка политики картонизации, по которой создана эта коробка.

`None` — тара родилась не из картонизации, ЛИБО той строки политики больше нет: ссылка обнуляется вместе с кандидатом, потому что запрет удалять кандидата из-за прошлогодней отгрузки — не та цена.

planned_at_receipt_id.description: ADR-046 — non-NULL when this container was minted by `CreateCaseLevelAsn` ahead of physical arrival (planned case or planned pallet); NULL for the dominant post-receive creation path. Populated from migration 128.

usage_policy_override.description: Исключение из `default_usage_policy` типа для этого экземпляра.

oneOf.description: The container arrived from another facility of the same company.
Тару породил план картонизации, а не человек и не приёмка.

Container has been minted by CreateCaseLevelAsn (ASN load) but the physical goods haven't arrived yet. Flipped to `Active` by ReceiveCaseLevelLine on first deposit. Container ops (Move/Restructure/Pick) should reject this status — the inventory_balances-empty guard is the de-facto enforcement until those commands gain explicit checks. See migration 164.
Коробка отгрузки, созданная картонизацией. Физика берётся не из мастера типов, а из строки политики, по которой её создали (`cartonization_policy_detail_id`).

oneOf.description: Bare override code (receipt / dimensionless).

params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

work_area_code.description: The work area scanned; blank or absent — the whole warehouse.

InventoryCountObservation.description: One scan or entry of the counter. Append-only; voided, never edited.

InventoryCountResult.description: What completing the task found for one identity.

movement_qty.description: The part of `expected_qty` the stock deltas between the snapshot and the completion made (a `Soft` count); 0 otherwise.

InventoryCountSnapshot.description: One identity the task is counted against.

variance_cause.description: ADR-093 (wms-app 132): why the accepted variance happened — a code of the `count_variance_cause` list — with what the supervisor added, and whether the accept was the system's own within tolerance.

SystemStockLine.description: One identity the system holds at a location, as the counter reads it.

schema.description: One location's count, as the counter and the supervisor see it.

count_only.description: What the counter counts here, in words, when it is not the whole location — a count of the item (Appendix G): "SKU A; lot L1". No quantity: the count stays blind.

expected.description: The stock the location is counted against — `None` while a blind count is being counted (spec §8, AC-03).

observations.description: What the counter recorded, voided rows included (history, spec §29).

results.description: What completing the task found; empty until it is counted.

Loc/Sku Abc - dependent type, code_list_value

`PartialEq`/`Eq` are unconditional (not `cfg(test)`) because `CandidateFilter::loc_abc` (phase 2a) holds a `PropRule<AbcRotationSpeed>`, and `CandidateFilter` derives `PartialEq, Eq` outside test code too.

One per warehouse schema, seeded as `INTRANSIT`; outside every other door — allocation, putaway, move, adjustment, receiving, the location advisory.

A pack station (post-pick spec §6, D-47, D-49; wms-app 066/067): the location where picked units wait for Verify / Repack. Goods arrive only by the Outbound Flow Router's decision, so no putaway, manual move or allocation targets it; picked stock is delivered into it.
A consolidation station (consolidation H1; wms-app 20261021191020/1): the location where packed boxes are put onto outbound pallets. Goods arrive only by the router's decision; never allocated from.

freeze_mode.description: `Hard` freezes the locations the policy's counts count; `Soft` lets stock move (count spec Appendix F).

sku_abc.description: `Items`: the SKUs of this ABC class (`sku.abc`).

trust_empty_confirmation.description: A location confirmed empty in passing counts as checked then (count spec Appendix L.6). Only a policy over locations reads it.

InventoryCountObservation.description: One scan or entry of the counter. Append-only; voided, never edited.

InventoryCountResult.description: What completing the task found for one identity.

movement_qty.description: The part of `expected_qty` the stock deltas between the snapshot and the completion made (a `Soft` count); 0 otherwise.

InventoryCountSnapshot.description: One identity the task is counted against.

variance_cause.description: ADR-093 (wms-app 132): why the accepted variance happened — a code of the `count_variance_cause` list — with what the supervisor added, and whether the accept was the system's own within tolerance.

SystemStockLine.description: One identity the system holds at a location, as the counter reads it.

schema.description: One location's count, as the counter and the supervisor see it.

count_only.description: What the counter counts here, in words, when it is not the whole location — a count of the item (Appendix G): "SKU A; lot L1". No quantity: the count stays blind.

expected.description: The stock the location is counted against — `None` while a blind count is being counted (spec §8, AC-03).

observations.description: What the counter recorded, voided rows included (history, spec §29).

results.description: What completing the task found; empty until it is counted.

stock_moved_under_count.description: A shift lead let an operation move stock under this count while it was frozen (owner's decision 2026-10-21 §6, `inventory_count_disturbance`). The counter is told because their number is then in doubt — the point of recording the override at all. Always `false` for a `Soft` count, which freezes nothing and so is never overridden.

system_stock.description: What the system holds here now, for the counter of an `Informed` count's first attempt while it is counted (count spec §8); `None` otherwise. A soft count's movements since its snapshot included.

check_kind.description: `Count`, or what the answer was against the stock: `ConfirmedEmpty` / `DeniedEmpty` / `EmptyAgainstStock`; or `UnexpectedStock`, an operator's report (Appendix M).

id.description: `C<task id>` for a count, `E<evidence id>` for an answer: one key across both.

operator.description: The operator's login, or `#<id>` for one the warehouse no longer has.

outcome.description: A count: its task's status (`Closed`, `Variance`, `Recounted` …). An answer the stock contradicted: `CountRequested`.

source.description: Which operation: the count's number and attempt (`INV-12 / 2`), the one that asked (`PickCommit #701`), or a report with what it named (`Report: LPN L-7 / SKU SKU002`).

system_qty.description: An answer: what the location held when it came (`SUM(qty)`).

schema.description:
A rule row of an allocation policy — migration 266's `sequence`/`active` plus the eight-column predicate (`allocation_type` … `qty_fit_rule`) and the four-deep `sort_1..sort_4` ordering. `sequence` is the execution order, never `rule_num`: `rule_num` is varchar(5) and sorts lexicographically ('10' before '2'), the same reasoning as `PutawayPolicyDetail::sequence` vs `step_num`.

`Deserialize` mirrors `PutawayPolicyDetail`'s own derive, and for the same reason (see that struct's doc): the allocation step page in `web-ui-server` has no warehouse database of its own and reads this row back over `get_allocation_policy_detail`/`list_allocation_policy_detail`, needing the eight predicate axes and the four sort ranks as TYPES — not as strings it would otherwise have to re-parse from a generic `serde_json::Value`.

StepDraft.description:
One step's unsaved draft, as the editor holds it: the columns the operator has changed, and nothing else.

The same shape the batch save sends (`SaveAllocationSteps::StepEdit`'s `step_id` + `fields`), on purpose — the screen holds ONE draft per step and hands the same thing to the read that narrates it and to the write that stores it. Two shapes would be two chances for the preview and the save to disagree about what the operator typed.

Clause.description:
One clause of a sentence, with the band that owns it.

`topic` is a plain string rather than the typed [`AllocationStepTopic`]: the consumer is a TypeScript component, and a lowercase band name is what it keys its four bands by. [`topic_name`] is the one place the mapping lives.

PipelineStep.description: One step of the pipeline: its fields, its words, and every verdict about it.

clauses.description: The running sentence, in the pieces the card's four bands need. A step the engine would skip gets only the sentence saying so — that is `narrate_allocation_step`'s rule, not this file's.

closed_by.description: The `rule_num` of the earlier step that leaves this one nothing to reserve, when there is one. A rule_num, not an id: it is what the operator reads on the card.

never_reserves.description:
What this step can never reserve even though the engine loads and runs it — a measured unit against a rule written for counted ones.

A SEPARATE list from `skip_reasons` and never to be merged with it: the card owes the operator two different sentences ("the engine skips this step" and "this step runs, but it can never fill anything"), and a reader told the first about a step the engine in fact ran would go looking for a refusal that does not exist.

skip_reasons.description: Why the engine would refuse this step when it LOADS the policy. Empty for a step that runs.

switched_off.description:
The sentence for a step the engine never loads because somebody switched it off, in the core's own words (`allocation_step_switched_off`) — `None` for a step that is on.

A sentence and not the bare `active` flag beside it: ADR-087 forbids the component to hold texts, so a screen handed only a boolean would have to author "switched off — the engine does not run this step" itself, and then there would be two authors of one line. `active` is still on the step for the toggle's own state.

version.description: This step's own optimistic lock — per step, never per policy, because two supervisors editing two different steps must not collide.

Run.description: The clause's words, cut into the values the operator chose and the rest. Concatenated, `text` of every run is the clause's own `text`, byte for byte.

bold.description: A value the operator picked — the card sets these in bold.

missing.description:
Words standing where a value the step NEEDS is not set — the card draws these amber, in place.

A FLAG and not a marker to match, because the marker is a translated phrase: the card used to be expected to find the gap by looking for its words in the clause, which needed the words sent to it, and nothing ever sent them. Never `true` together with `bold`.

StepFields.description:
The thirteen card fields, under their own column names.

Spelled out rather than embedding [`AllocationPolicyDetail`] whole: the card edits exactly these, and a wire shape that also carried `add_who` / `mod_when` / `allocation_policy_id` would invite a draft to send them back.

schema.description: One allocation policy's pipeline, with everything the card draws beside each step.

lifecycle.description: Drives editor affordances: only `Draft` accepts header/step writes.

next_rule_num.description: What the system will call the next step the operator adds. Shown on the "+ Add step" affordance BEFORE the add, which is why it is here and not only in the add command's answer.

policy_version.description: The policy's own optimistic lock — what a reorder must echo back.

steps.description: Every step of the policy, switched-off ones included, in execution order (`sequence`, never `rule_num` — that is `varchar(5)` and sorts '10' before '2').

OrderStatus.description:
The header's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.1): `New → Allocated → Released → Picked → Closed`, every working rung with a `Partially` form, `Cancelled` reachable until things are picked. Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Status is a DERIVED column: the truth lives in the lines' counters and the header's markers (`released_at`/`cancelled_at`/`closed_at`); `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order::derive_order_status` recomputes it inside every mutating transaction.

OrderLineStatus.description:
The line's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.2). A line with no reservations is `NotAllocated` — including after an unallocate — so the status honestly answers "is there stock under this line?". Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Derived, like the header's: `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order:: derive_line_status` recomputes it from the counters inside every mutating transaction. The `Released` rung is measured by picks handed to a task (`pick_detail.status = 'Released'`) — `wms_tasks::service::generate:: generate_tasks_for_picks` (task 7) is that writer. On a LAUNCHED order it dispatches, in the SAME transaction, every live pick of the order that does not carry a task yet — not just the ones the current `release` / `Allocate` pass reserved itself, which would forever skip a pick that a pre-launch `Allocate` (spec §3.1) had already reserved before the gate let dispatch happen. So this rung is reached routinely, not merely a future special case of the picking phase.

allocation_policy_id.description: Frozen allocation-policy identity. Nullable during expand/backfill; new-runtime writes become mandatory only in the contract migration.

pack_requested.description: `true`: the customer ordered `pack_id`, and the line is reserved only from stock of that pack. `false`: `pack_id` is the SKU's pack, put there because the order named none, and stock of any pack of the SKU is a candidate.

pick_instruction.description: One-off pick instruction for this line, from the ERP (wms-app 044): shown on its picks and acknowledged before a pick commits (RF `PICKINS`).

qty_allocated.description: Always 0 in Phase 1 — written by allocation in Phase 2.

qty_ordered.description: All five counters are in BASE units.

qty_picked.description: Always 0 in Phase 1 — written by picking in Phase 3.

qty_shipped.description: Always 0 in Phase 1 — written by shipping in Phase 3.

uom_factor.description: `pack_item.base_qty` snapshot taken when the line was created. Stored — unlike on `receipt_detail` — so a later `pack_item` edit cannot rewrite what a historical line meant.

version.description: Per-line OCC, independent of the header's version.

blocked_by_dropped_step.description: Sum, across every line, of [`crate::allocation::LineAllocationPlan::blocked_by_dropped_step`] — base units `short` includes that were never searched for at all, because the only step of some line's policy naming that UOM rung failed to parse (round-2 review finding: without this, a broken policy step and a genuinely empty warehouse produced the identical `short` number). Zero on the common path.

cartonization.description:
Что посчитала картонизация: номер плана и сколько в нём коробок, размещений и неразмещённого. `None`, когда считать было нечего или когда заказ уже запущен.

`default`, чтобы сохранённый идемпотентный повтор, записанный до появления поля, продолжал разбираться.

cartonization_error.description: `Some`, когда картонизация не удалась. Резервирование при этом УСПЕШНО: план — подсказка складу, а не условие отгрузки. Но молчать нельзя — иначе экран покажет успех, а склад обнаружит отсутствие коробок в момент отбора.

contention_deferred.description: Quantity deferred because another transaction held the inventory lock. Default preserves idempotent results stored by older builds.

dispatched_tasks.description:
Tasks THIS pass handed out — one per live pick of the order that had none yet (see the dispatch comment in [`allocate_order_lines`]). Empty before launch: a pre-launch Allocate reserves, it does not dispatch.

The screen's toast reads it. A second Release on a `PartiallyReleased` order reserves nothing new — `allocated 0, short 0` — and its whole point is the tasks, which the toast could not name while the generator's answer was thrown away here (owner, 2026-09-12). `default`, so an idempotent replay stored before the field existed still deserializes.

short.description: Quantity that could not be reserved because the eligible stock did not exist (as opposed to being temporarily locked).

status.description: The header status AS DERIVED after the pass — `Allocated` / `PartiallyAllocated` before launch, `Released` / `PartiallyReleased` on a launched order (release's own nested pass runs after `released_at` is already written, so it reads the same ladder). The screen patches its copy of the order from this (spec §6.3).

OrderStatus.description:
The header's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.1): `New → Allocated → Released → Picked → Closed`, every working rung with a `Partially` form, `Cancelled` reachable until things are picked. Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Status is a DERIVED column: the truth lives in the lines' counters and the header's markers (`released_at`/`cancelled_at`/`closed_at`); `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order::derive_order_status` recomputes it inside every mutating transaction.

master_data_divergences.description: What stands was taken as written; where today's master data says otherwise, it is named here for master-data review (an executed unit whose size, weight or rotation rule changed). Empty for a plan that builds on nothing. `default`: a result stored before this field still reads (idempotent replays).

auto_allocation.description: What release's own allocation half did — `allocated`/`short` report the pass that ran in this same transaction. Release ALWAYS attempts it now (spec §8.2), so this is `None` only when the attempt itself FAILED — see `auto_allocation_error`. Kept as an `Option` under its original name so existing callers keep deserializing unchanged.

auto_allocation_error.description: `Some` when the allocation half failed (review round 1) — a misconfigured policy is the expected case, but any error `allocate_order_lines` returns lands here. `release` still succeeds when this is set: see the module doc ("A failed allocation pass does not fail the release"). Exactly one of this and `auto_allocation` is always `Some`.

status.description: The header status AS DERIVED at the end of this command's own transaction — `Released` when the allocation half covered every live line, `PartiallyReleased` when it did not (spec §2.2). The screen patches its copy of the order from this instead of assuming the launch always lands on the full form (§6.3's stale-status bug).

AllocatedPosition.description:
One position [`plan_line_allocation`] found for a line — the wire-facing projection of [`crate::allocation::PlannedDraw`]. Its own type, not a re-export: `balance_id`'s internal-engine framing is implementation detail a caller of a *preview* should not have to know exists as a separate concept from `take`; here it is just "how much, from where."

`uom` (проход 2, задача 5) IS surfaced, though — it is the STEP's unit [`plan_line_allocation`] planned this draw under, the exact value [`reserve_draw`] writes onto `pick_detail.uom` when the real command reserves it. A multi-step policy plans the same line's need across several uoms (spec §4.2's PL/CS/IP/EA cascade); a caller of the preview needs to see which unit each position will pick in, not just the line's own (order-level) `uom` on [`LineAllocationPreview`] — that field answers "what did the customer order in," this one answers "what will THIS pick be counted in."

AllocationTraceDetail.description: Cost level for planner explainability. Normal allocation always uses `Summary`; only an explicitly requested diagnostic preview uses `Full`.

allocated.description: Sum of `positions[].qty` — what the plan found, not a guarantee (see [`AllocationPreview`]'s own doc comment).

allocation_policy_id.description: Frozen policy snapshot used by the shared planner. Absent only for a line with no remaining demand and no historical snapshot.

blocked_by_dropped_step.description: This line's own [`crate::allocation::LineAllocationPlan:: blocked_by_dropped_step`] — a subset of `short` a caller can use to tell "the policy needs fixing" apart from "there is no stock." Zero on the common path.

need.description: `qty_to_allocate()` at read time, floored at zero.

steps.description: Typed step-by-step explanation. Full detail adds aggregate rejection counts to each evaluated step; it never returns inventory rows.

OrderStatus.description:
The header's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.1): `New → Allocated → Released → Picked → Closed`, every working rung with a `Partially` form, `Cancelled` reachable until things are picked. Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Status is a DERIVED column: the truth lives in the lines' counters and the header's markers (`released_at`/`cancelled_at`/`closed_at`); `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order::derive_order_status` recomputes it inside every mutating transaction.

StepDecision.description: One step's decision in the shared planner result. It contains quantities and stable codes only; no SQL fragments or candidate inventory rows.

StepRejectionCounts.description: Typed Full-preview rejection counters. The database counters form a waterfall; the selector counters are the real pure predicates applied after candidate loading.

shelf_life_failed.description: Lots rejected on their dates: expired, below the reserve boundary (today + max(`min_shelf_life_on_pick`, `shelf_life`)), or missing an expiration the SKU requires.

StepVerdict.description: Stable wire verdict for one policy step. Configuration defects never become a verdict: policy loading still returns an error.

schema.description: What [`preview_allocate_order`] returns. Deliberately its OWN type, not [`AllocateShipmentOrderResult`] with `new_version`/`picks` left empty — a preview never reserves anything, so it has no version to echo and no `pick_detail` ids to report; a shared type would carry two fields whose only value here is "always empty," which is not a description of what this command returns, it is a description of what it does NOT do.

advisory.description: Preview is observational and can be stale immediately after the read.

blocked_by_dropped_step.description: Sum of `lines[].blocked_by_dropped_step` — see that field's own doc.

order_status.description: Carried through so a caller previewing an unlaunched order (see below) can tell the rungs apart without a second round trip.

A second Release on a `PartiallyReleased` order reserves nothing new — `allocated 0, short 0` — and its whole point is the tasks, which the toast could not name while the generator's answer was thrown away here (owner, 2026-09-12). `default`, so an idempotent replay stored before the field existed still deserializes.

OrderLineStatus.description:
The line's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.2). A line with no reservations is `NotAllocated` — including after an unallocate — so the status honestly answers "is there stock under this line?". Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Derived, like the header's: `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order:: derive_line_status` recomputes it from the counters inside every mutating transaction. The `Released` rung is measured by picks handed to a task (`pick_detail.status = 'Released'`) — `wms_tasks::service::generate:: generate_tasks_for_picks` (task 7) is that writer. On a LAUNCHED order it dispatches, in the SAME transaction, every live pick of the order that does not carry a task yet — not just the ones the current `release` / `Allocate` pass reserved itself, which would forever skip a pick that a pre-launch `Allocate` (spec §3.1) had already reserved before the gate let dispatch happen. So this rung is reached routinely, not merely a future special case of the picking phase.

The affected LINE's stored status after the same derivation — the shape [`CancelLineQtyResult::line_status`] already reports for the other line-touching command family.

order_status.description:
The header status AS DERIVED after the release, in this command's own transaction — same contract as [`CancelOrderAllocationResult::status`] (`cancel_allocation.rs`): the screen patches its copy of the order from this (spec §6.3) instead of keeping whatever it showed before. A delete can move the header (a fully-`Released` order loses a pick → `PartiallyReleased`), and a result that stayed silent about it left the header box stale until a full reopen — the owner's live find, 2026-08-24.

escalated_at.description: Когда задача ушла супервайзеру: отказов набралось до порога `TASK_SKIP_ESCALATE_AFTER`. Пока стоит — выдача её не отдаёт никому.

refused_count.description: Сколько раз от задачи ОТКАЗАЛИСЬ (сдача в счёт не идёт). Растёт в [`TaskBmc::release_to_pool`], обнуляется только переназначением супервайзером ([`TaskBmc::reassign_cas`]) — миграция 307.

return_kind.description: КАК задача в последний раз вернулась в пул: `Refused` (отказ оператора), `HandedBack` (сдача), `Seized` (изъял супервайзер), `Expired` (истекла аренда). `skip_reason` пишут все трое, у кого есть причина, и без этого поля доска выдавала бы причину изъятия за причину отказа (миграция 308). Снимается вместе с `skip_reason`, когда задачу снова берут.

weight.description:
Вес запаса задачи на момент её создания — единственная формула веса (`pack::StockWeights`), скопированная, как и `qty` (wms-app 340).

`None` — взвесить было нечем (`PhysicalMetric::Unknown`): ни у базовой строки упаковки, ни у карточки товара веса нет. Такая задача проходит любой предел грузоподъёмности — проверка, которой нечего сравнивать, не имеет права отказывать (wms-app 341, спека физических измерений §9.2). Ноль больше не значит «неизвестно»: он сравнивается как число.

workstation_completed_by.description: Real web executor of source-owned workstation Pick completion. A pooled task can finish without pretending it had an RF assignment.

oneOf.description: Sitting in the dispatch pool. Dispatch claims it; source-owned manual Pick completion may also finish it together with physical inventory.
Handed to an operator by `claim_next`. Only the methods in [`TaskBmc`]'s "dispatch write surface" move a task out of it — there is no generic `update` on this BMC, by the rule stated there.

**Declared, and written by nothing.** Its one writer was `TaskBmc::cancel_in_work`, deleted on 2026-09-04 when the owner ruled that a task whose pick is removed is removed too, whatever state it is in (see `TaskBmc::delete_for_removed_source`). The variant stays because spec §9 declares a status set up front — do not go hunting for the code that writes it.
One location of an inventory count, one attempt (source `inventory_count_task`, wms-app 062). No quantity: the count is blind.

VerificationView.description: What the card must prove about the source of a pick, and how far the operator has got.

blocked.description: The wire code of the refusal that makes the pick uncommittable: `SOURCE_EXPIRED` — the reserved lot fell below the SKU's minimum shelf life on pick after it was reserved (ruling D5; the pick is shorted to zero with the reason `EXPIRED`, or rejected); or `SOURCE_NOT_PHYSICALLY_IDENTIFIABLE` — the source cannot be told apart by what is physically there (shorted to zero, rejected or skipped). blocked_message.description: What the card says about `blocked`, in the reader's language: why the pick cannot be committed and the way out a short has. Set exactly when `blocked` is; the terminal prints it as is.

episode_id.description: The caller's usable open episode, if one exists. A confirmation opens it; this view never does.

next.description: What the operator proves next; `None` when the plan is satisfied (or blocked).

satisfied.description: The plan's evidence already proven, in plan order.

stale.description: The caller's open episode proves another source, or belongs to another ownership (R8, R12): the plan restarts, and the first confirmation cancels that episode and opens a new one.

assignment.description: Carrier work instead of a single task. ABSENT (not `null`) on every discrete answer, so the discrete wire is exactly what it was.

drop_to_close.description: The caller's open pick pallet WITH goods, when the answer is not a discrete task that goes onto it — another order's task, a task of its order going to another location than the pallet (owner cross-review 2026-10-06, D-2), no work, or carrier work: the RF closes it first (spec §4.5, PICK13). params.summary: Control-plane envelope (idempotency_key, expected_version, acknowledged_overrides — bare integer codes for receipt, or {code, subject} override pairs for move). Optional fields per ADR-058 D-3 semantic gating.

count_freeze_grant_id.description: A shift lead's grant (`supervisor_override_grant`) authorising this confirmation out of a location an open Hard count is counting (owner's decision 2026-10-21 §6). The SAME single-use grant the move and the adjustment redeem. Absent from the wire when `None`, so an ordinary commit serialises — and hashes — exactly as before.

drop_id.description: Discrete (CollectToRoot): the caller's open pick pallet — its CONTAINER id, as `pick_drop_open` answered it. Absent from the wire when `None`, so a discrete request serializes — and hashes — exactly as before slice 4.

instructions_acknowledged.description: The picker read the pick's instructions (RF `PICKINS`). Required when the pick has any (`picking::instructions`); the commit re-derives that from the locked rows, it does not trust the client. Absent from the wire when false, so the idempotency hash of a request without it is what it always was.

target_container_code.description: A pick a live assignment holds (DirectToTarget): the box the operator scanned at its position — must be that position's box (R5).

OrderLineStatus.description:
The line's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.2). A line with no reservations is `NotAllocated` — including after an unallocate — so the status honestly answers "is there stock under this line?". Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Derived, like the header's: `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order:: derive_line_status` recomputes it from the counters inside every mutating transaction. The `Released` rung is measured by picks handed to a task (`pick_detail.status = 'Released'`) — `wms_tasks::service::generate:: generate_tasks_for_picks` (task 7) is that writer. On a LAUNCHED order it dispatches, in the SAME transaction, every live pick of the order that does not carry a task yet — not just the ones the current `release` / `Allocate` pass reserved itself, which would forever skip a pick that a pre-launch `Allocate` (spec §3.1) had already reserved before the gate let dispatch happen. So this rung is reached routinely, not merely a future special case of the picking phase.

OrderStatus.description:
The header's status ladder (migration 285, spec 2026-08-19 §1.1): `New → Allocated → Released → Picked → Closed`, every working rung with a `Partially` form, `Cancelled` reachable until things are picked. Variant order matches the Postgres enum's own order, which IS the ladder.

Status is a DERIVED column: the truth lives in the lines' counters and the header's markers (`released_at`/`cancelled_at`/`closed_at`); `wms_outbound::domain::shipment_order::derive_order_status` recomputes it inside every mutating transaction.

oneOf.description: Positions are being bound to physical boxes.
Every position is bound; the route may start.
A live reservation — the qty this row carries is set aside and must be released by cancel/short before the balance can be reused.
Handed to a picker/task; still counts as reserved.

DEAD VALUE — nothing assigns it anymore (status-machine arc, owner decision 2026-08-19 §8.5): a released reservation is DELETED, its audit is the `process.order.line_allocation_released` event. The label stays here and in SQL only because Postgres cannot `ALTER TYPE ... DROP VALUE`, and rows written before the arc may still carry it.

Closed with `qty_picked < qty` — the short-pick outcome. Kept as a ROW (unlike Cancelled): a short records an actual pick that happened, not an intention that was withdrawn. Where the shortfall was found is the row's `short_place` (set exactly while `Shorted`): [`PickShortPlace::Shelf`] — at the source location, nothing of the shortfall was picked (`qty - qty_picked` never left the shelf); [`PickShortPlace::Tote`] — in a tote at a station (S0 §7.4): all of `qty` WAS picked from the shelf and went to Lost with the short, and `qty_picked` is 0 because none of it is the order's any more. Alike otherwise; the balance per root (§7.7) counts only the tote's.

Taken from the shelf into a tote bound for a station (spec 2026-10-11 picking S0, §7 О-3): the task's work is done (П-3) — its task is closed — but the pick is not: the wall places it into a position's box through `picking::placement` (`Picked`), or closes it there (`Shorted`, `Returned`). Its goods lie in `held_in_container_id`. Never a dispatch / cart / continuation candidate; not a live reservation (`qty_allocated` left the source at the commit).

Returned to storage (spec S0 §7.5, О-5): the wall took the pick back off picking (`record_unstaged`, R-14) — its goods became free where the wall put them. Terminal; `qty_picked = 0`. refused_count.description: Сколько раз от задачи ОТКАЗАЛИСЬ (сдача в счёт не идёт). Растёт в [`TaskBmc::release_to_pool`], обнуляется только переназначением супервайзером ([`TaskBmc::reassign_cas`]) — миграция 307.

return_kind.description: КАК задача в последний раз вернулась в пул: `Refused` (отказ оператора), `HandedBack` (сдача), `Seized` (изъял супервайзер), `Expired` (истекла аренда). `skip_reason` пишут все трое, у кого есть причина, и без этого поля доска выдавала бы причину изъятия за причину отказа (миграция 308). weight.description:
Вес запаса задачи на момент её создания — единственная формула веса (`pack::StockWeights`), скопированная, как и `qty` (wms-app 340).

schema.description:
A supervisor delivers a `Delivering` cart on its holder's behalf (ruling D3): the holder left the shift, is ill, or their account is gone, and the picked goods must still reach their location. So is a cart the supervisor dissolved with goods on its carrier (the only exit ruling D1 leaves a started cart). The carrier goes to the assignment's delivery location as the row has it — frozen at start, or retargeted by a supervisor (`pick_destination_retarget`) — with no scan; the policy's `Complete` finishes it where it stands, unless a supervisor retargeted it because that location died: then at the location they named. Recorded with the supervisor as `delivered_by` and on every journal row.

A `stateful_command` on `pick_assignment.version` (`.claude/rules/api-versioning-and-idempotency.md`): the supervisor decides on what the board shows — a cart waiting for delivery, its location; had they seen the holder back on it, or another location, they would not press this. A stale version answers code 40 with the current state.

LocType.description: LocType — dependent type, mirrors PostgreSQL `loc_type` enum. Migration 143 added 7 hold-stage zone purposes (QC/Damage/Rtv/Destroy/ Returns/Stage/Lost) used by Move primitive §3.2.1 destination authorization.

oneOf.description: The location of open discrete pick pallets (the pick-pallet wms-app migrations): goods on an operator's forks between the pick and the pallet's close. One per warehouse schema, seeded as `INTRANSIT`; outside every other door — allocation, putaway, move, adjustment, receiving, the location advisory.

A pack station (post-pick spec §6, D-47, D-49; wms-app 066/067): the location where picked units wait for Verify / Repack. Goods arrive only by the Outbound Flow Router's decision, so no putaway, manual move or allocation targets it; picked stock is delivered into it.
A consolidation station (consolidation H1; wms-app 20261021191020/1): the location where packed boxes are put onto outbound pallets. Goods arrive only by the router's decision; never allocated from.
A pick that empties its location does nothing more.
The emptied location is counted (count spec Appendix D, PICK_TO_ZERO).
The operator is asked whether the location is empty; an answer the stock contradicts asks for a count (count spec Appendix L).
The card shows the item; nothing is asked of the operator.
The operator confirms the item by scanning it.
The server picks the proof from the physical structure of the source.
One lot per location is the proof.
`owners.picking_toloc`, else the order's tasks' `to_location` when they agree (ADR-091) — the only chain today.

PickingPolicySections.description: Every field is required on the wire: an update that left the pallet-drop list out would otherwise reset a narrowed list without a word, and one that left a Confirmation value out would loosen what the operator proves at the source. Only an assignment snapshot taken before those settings existed reads them as their defaults ([`PickingPolicySections::deserialize_snapshot`]).

pick_to_zero.description: What a full pick that leaves its source location holding no stock does (section «Завершение»): nothing, count the location (count spec Appendix D, PICK_TO_ZERO) or ask the operator whether it is empty (Appendix L, ZERO_CONFIRMATION).

source_location_confirmation.description: Spec §7, section «Подтверждение»: what the operator proves at the source. Not part of the grouping shape (`shape_eq` ignores them).

oneOf.description: The operator scans the reserved LPN whenever the source has one.

schema.description: Work area — a named set of putaway zones where an operator is allowed to work (task-manager pass 2, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-work-areas-operator-profile-design.md`). It is the unit task distribution will filter by: an operator's rights are a grid of `task type × work area`, and a task reaches its area through `task.from_location → location.putawayzone → work_area_zone`. Renamed from `facility` (owner decision 2026-08-27); the columns that make it an area — the concurrent-task limit, "may hand a task back" — arrived in step 2 (wms-app 315), and the rules that read them come in step 6.

allow_task_release.description: May an operator hand a task back here (Infor "Sign Off Allowed"). Read by `TaskService::skip_task_in_area` since step 6 — it gates BOTH doors, the hand-back and the refusal; without a named area the warehouse default (`TASK_ALLOW_RELEASE_DEFAULT`) rules instead.

consolidation_station_location.description: The area's consolidation station (consolidation H1; wms-app 20261021191021): the `Consolidation` location where its packed units are put onto outbound pallets. `None` — packed units are `Completed` as before.

max_concurrent_tasks.description: Tasks one operator may hold at once inside this area — only when the terminal names the area (spec §4.1). Read by `TaskService::claim_one_in_area` since step 6; without a named area the warehouse default (`TASK_MAX_CONCURRENT_DEFAULT`) rules instead.

pack_station_location.description: The area's pack station (wms-app 065; post-pick spec О-1, D-55): the `Pack` location its carriers are delivered to when their units go to packing. `None` — no station: picking delivers as before. Only a `Pack` location (wms-app 079).

picking_policy_code.description: Code of the picking policy this area works by (its published revision); `None` = `DISCRETE`. Read side only — assignment goes through `PickingPolicyBmc::assign_to_work_area` (wms-app 042).

oneOf.description: Sitting in the dispatch pool. Dispatch claims it; source-owned manual Pick completion may also finish it together with physical inventory.
Handed to an operator by `claim_next`. Only the methods in [`TaskBmc`]'s "dispatch write surface" move a task out of it — there is no generic `update` on this BMC, by the rule stated there.

**Declared, and written by nothing.** Its one writer was `TaskBmc::cancel_in_work`, deleted on 2026-09-04 when the owner ruled that a task whose pick is removed is removed too, whatever state it is in (see `TaskBmc::delete_for_removed_source`). The variant stays because spec §9 declares a status set up front — do not go hunting for the code that writes it.

escalated_at.description: Когда задача ушла супервайзеру: отказов набралось до порога `TASK_SKIP_ESCALATE_AFTER`. Пока стоит — выдача её не отдаёт никому.

refused_count.description: Сколько раз от задачи ОТКАЗАЛИСЬ (сдача в счёт не идёт). Растёт в [`TaskBmc::release_to_pool`], обнуляется только переназначением супервайзером ([`TaskBmc::reassign_cas`]) — миграция 307.

return_kind.description: КАК задача в последний раз вернулась в пул: `Refused` (отказ оператора), `HandedBack` (сдача), `Seized` (изъял супервайзер), `Expired` (истекла аренда). `skip_reason` пишут все трое, у кого есть причина, и без этого поля доска выдавала бы причину изъятия за причину отказа (миграция 308). Снимается вместе с `skip_reason`, когда задачу снова берут.

weight.description:
Вес запаса задачи на момент её создания — единственная формула веса (`pack::StockWeights`), скопированная, как и `qty` (wms-app 340).

`None` — взвесить было нечем (`PhysicalMetric::Unknown`): ни у базовой строки упаковки, ни у карточки товара веса нет. Такая задача проходит любой предел грузоподъёмности — проверка, которой нечего сравнивать, не имеет права отказывать (wms-app 341, спека физических измерений §9.2). Ноль больше не значит «неизвестно»: он сравнивается как число.

`None` — взвесить было нечем (`PhysicalMetric::Unknown`): ни у базовой строки упаковки, ни у карточки товара веса нет. Такая задача проходит любой предел грузоподъёмности — проверка, которой нечего сравнивать, не имеет права отказывать (wms-app 341, спека физических измерений §9.2). Ноль больше не значит «неизвестно»: он сравнивается как число.

oneOf.description: Sitting in the dispatch pool. Dispatch claims it; source-owned manual Pick completion may also finish it together with physical inventory.
Handed to an operator by `claim_next`. Only the methods in [`TaskBmc`]'s "dispatch write surface" move a task out of it — there is no generic `update` on this BMC, by the rule stated there.

**Declared, and written by nothing.** Its one writer was `TaskBmc::cancel_in_work`, deleted on 2026-09-04 when the owner ruled that a task whose pick is removed is removed too, whatever state it is in (see `TaskBmc::delete_for_removed_source`). The variant stays because spec §9 declares a status set up front — do not go hunting for the code that writes it.
One location of an inventory count, one attempt (source `inventory_count_task`, wms-app 062). No quantity: the count is blind.
